2:122.ar: يَٰبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَتِيَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنۡعَمۡتُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَأَنِّي فَضَّلۡتُكُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
2:122.en: O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds

2:123.ar: وَٱتَّقُواْ يَوۡمࣰ ا لَّا تَجۡزِي نَفۡسٌ عَن نَّفۡسࣲ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يُقۡبَلُ مِنۡهَا عَدۡلࣱ وَلَا تَنفَعُهَا شَفَٰعَةࣱ وَلَا هُمۡ يُنصَرُونَ
2:123.en: And fear a Day when no soul will suffice for another soul at all, and no compensation will be accepted from it, nor will any intercession benefit it, nor will they be aided

2:124.ar: ۞وَإِذِ ٱبۡتَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ رَبُّهُۥ بِكَلِمَٰتࣲ فَأَتَمَّهُنَّۖ قَالَ إِنِّي جَاعِلُكَ لِلنَّاسِ إِمَامࣰ اۖ قَالَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِيۖ قَالَ لَا يَنَالُ عَهۡدِي ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:124.en: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham was tried by his Lord with commands and he fulfilled them. [Allah] said, "Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people." [Abraham] said, "And of my descendants?" [Allah] said, "My covenant does not include the wrongdoers

2:125.ar: وَإِذۡ جَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡبَيۡتَ مَثَابَةࣰ لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَمۡنࣰ ا وَٱتَّخِذُواْ مِن مَّقَامِ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ مُصَلࣰّ ىۖ وَعَهِدۡنَآ إِلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلَ أَن طَهِّرَا بَيۡتِيَ لِلطَّآئِفِينَ وَٱلۡعَٰكِفِينَ وَٱلرُّكَّعِ ٱلسُّجُودِ
2:125.en: And [mention] when We made the House a place of return for the people and [a place of] security. And take, [O believers], from the standing place of Abraham a place of prayer. And We charged Abraham and Ishmael, [saying], "Purify My House for those who perform Tawaf and those who are staying [there] for worship and those who bow and prostrate [in prayer]

2:126.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ ٱجۡعَلۡ هَٰذَا بَلَدًا ءَامِنࣰ ا وَٱرۡزُقۡ أَهۡلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ مِنۡهُم بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۚ قَالَ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَأُمَتِّعُهُۥ قَلِيلࣰ ا ثُمَّ أَضۡطَرُّهُۥٓ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ ٱلنَّارِۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
2:126.en: And [mention] when Abraham said, "My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits - whoever of them believes in Allah and the Last Day." [Allah] said. "And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little; then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination

2:127.ar: وَإِذۡ يَرۡفَعُ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ ٱلۡقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلُ رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلۡ مِنَّآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
2:127.en: And [mention] when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House and [with him] Ishmael, [saying], "Our Lord, accept [this] from us. Indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing

2:128.ar: رَبَّنَا وَٱجۡعَلۡنَا مُسۡلِمَيۡنِ لَكَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِنَآ أُمَّةࣰ مُّسۡلِمَةࣰ لَّكَ وَأَرِنَا مَنَاسِكَنَا وَتُبۡ عَلَيۡنَآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:128.en: Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful

2:129.ar: رَبَّنَا وَٱبۡعَثۡ فِيهِمۡ رَسُولࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِكَ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَيُزَكِّيهِمۡۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
2:129.en: Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and wisdom and purify them. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise

2:130.ar: وَمَن يَرۡغَبُ عَن مِّلَّةِ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ إِلَّا مَن سَفِهَ نَفۡسَهُۥۚ وَلَقَدِ ٱصۡطَفَيۡنَٰهُ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَإِنَّهُۥ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ لَمِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
2:130.en: And who would be averse to the religion of Abraham except one who makes a fool of himself. And We had chosen him in this world, and indeed he, in the Hereafter, will be among the righteous

2:131.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ لَهُۥ رَبُّهُۥٓ أَسۡلِمۡۖ قَالَ أَسۡلَمۡتُ لِرَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
2:131.en: When his Lord said to him, "Submit", he said "I have submitted [in Islam] to the Lord of the worlds

2:132.ar: وَوَصَّىٰ بِهَآ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ بَنِيهِ وَيَعۡقُوبُ يَٰبَنِيَّ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصۡطَفَىٰ لَكُمُ ٱلدِّينَ فَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنتُم مُّسۡلِمُونَ
2:132.en: And Abraham instructed his sons [to do the same] and [so did] Jacob, [saying], "O my sons, indeed Allah has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims

2:133.ar: أَمۡ كُنتُمۡ شُهَدَآءَ إِذۡ حَضَرَ يَعۡقُوبَ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ إِذۡ قَالَ لِبَنِيهِ مَا تَعۡبُدُونَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِيۖ قَالُواْ نَعۡبُدُ إِلَٰهَكَ وَإِلَٰهَ ءَابَآئِكَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَ إِلَٰهࣰ ا وَٰحِدࣰ ا وَنَحۡنُ لَهُۥ مُسۡلِمُونَ
2:133.en: Or were you witnesses when death approached Jacob, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac - one God. And we are Muslims [in submission] to Him

2:134.ar: تِلۡكَ أُمَّةࣱ قَدۡ خَلَتۡۖ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتۡ وَلَكُم مَّا كَسَبۡتُمۡۖ وَلَا تُسۡـَٔلُونَ عَمَّا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
2:134.en: That was a nation which has passed on. It will have [the consequence of] what it earned, and you will have what you have earned. And you will not be asked about what they used to do

2:135.ar: وَقَالُواْ كُونُواْ هُودًا أَوۡ نَصَٰرَىٰ تَهۡتَدُواْۗ قُلۡ بَلۡ مِلَّةَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ حَنِيفࣰ اۖ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ
2:135.en: They say, "Be Jews or Christians [so] you will be guided." Say, "Rather, [we follow] the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists

2:136.ar: قُولُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡنَا وَمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَ وَٱلۡأَسۡبَاطِ وَمَآ أُوتِيَ مُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰ وَمَآ أُوتِيَ ٱلنَّبِيُّونَ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيۡنَ أَحَدࣲ مِّنۡهُمۡ وَنَحۡنُ لَهُۥ مُسۡلِمُونَ
2:136.en: Say, [O believers], "We have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Descendants and what was given to Moses and Jesus and what was given to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him

2:137.ar: فَإِنۡ ءَامَنُواْ بِمِثۡلِ مَآ ءَامَنتُم بِهِۦ فَقَدِ ٱهۡتَدَواْۖ وَّإِن تَوَلَّوۡاْ فَإِنَّمَا هُمۡ فِي شِقَاقࣲۖ فَسَيَكۡفِيكَهُمُ ٱللَّهُۚ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
2:137.en: So if they believe in the same as you believe in, then they have been [rightly] guided; but if they turn away, they are only in dissension, and Allah will be sufficient for you against them. And He is the Hearing, the Knowing

2:138.ar: صِبۡغَةَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَنۡ أَحۡسَنُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ صِبۡغَةࣰۖ وَنَحۡنُ لَهُۥ عَٰبِدُونَ
2:138.en: [And say, "Ours is] the religion of Allah. And who is better than Allah in [ordaining] religion? And we are worshippers of Him

2:139.ar: قُلۡ أَتُحَآجُّونَنَا فِي ٱللَّهِ وَهُوَ رَبُّنَا وَرَبُّكُمۡ وَلَنَآ أَعۡمَٰلُنَا وَلَكُمۡ أَعۡمَٰلُكُمۡ وَنَحۡنُ لَهُۥ مُخۡلِصُونَ
2:139.en: Say, [O Muhammad], "Do you argue with us about Allah while He is our Lord and your Lord? For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. And we are sincere [in deed and intention] to Him

2:140.ar: أَمۡ تَقُولُونَ إِنَّ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَ وَٱلۡأَسۡبَاطَ كَانُواْ هُودًا أَوۡ نَصَٰرَىٰۗ قُلۡ ءَأَنتُمۡ أَعۡلَمُ أَمِ ٱللَّهُۗ وَمَنۡ أَظۡلَمُ مِمَّن كَتَمَ شَهَٰدَةً عِندَهُۥ مِنَ ٱللَّهِۗ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
2:140.en: Or do you say that Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Descendants were Jews or Christians? Say, "Are you more knowing or is Allah?" And who is more unjust than one who conceals a testimony he has from Allah? And Allah is not unaware of what you do

2:141.ar: تِلۡكَ أُمَّةࣱ قَدۡ خَلَتۡۖ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتۡ وَلَكُم مَّا كَسَبۡتُمۡۖ وَلَا تُسۡـَٔلُونَ عَمَّا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
2:141.en: That is a nation which has passed on. It will have [the consequence of] what it earned, and you will have what you have earned. And you will not be asked about what they used to do

2:142.ar: ۞سَيَقُولُ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَا وَلَّىٰهُمۡ عَن قِبۡلَتِهِمُ ٱلَّتِي كَانُواْ عَلَيۡهَاۚ قُل لِّلَّهِ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقُ وَٱلۡمَغۡرِبُۚ يَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطࣲ مُّسۡتَقِيمࣲ‏
2:142.en: The foolish among the people will say, "What has turned them away from their qiblah, which they used to face?" Say, "To Allah belongs the east and the west. He guides whom He wills to a straight path

2:143.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ أُمَّةࣰ وَسَطࣰ ا لِّتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ شَهِيدࣰ اۗ وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡقِبۡلَةَ ٱلَّتِي كُنتَ عَلَيۡهَآ إِلَّا لِنَعۡلَمَ مَن يَتَّبِعُ ٱلرَّسُولَ مِمَّن يَنقَلِبُ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيۡهِۚ وَإِن كَانَتۡ لَكَبِيرَةً إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَى ٱللَّهُۗ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَٰنَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِٱلنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
2:143.en: And thus we have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you. And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels. And indeed, it is difficult except for those whom Allah has guided. And never would Allah have caused you to lose your faith. Indeed Allah is, to the people, Kind and Merciful

2:144.ar: قَدۡ نَرَىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجۡهِكَ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِۖ فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ قِبۡلَةࣰ تَرۡضَىٰهَاۚ فَوَلِّ وَجۡهَكَ شَطۡرَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۚ وَحَيۡثُ مَا كُنتُمۡ فَوَلُّواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ شَطۡرَهُۥۗ وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ لَيَعۡلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡۗ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا يَعۡمَلُونَ
2:144.en: We have certainly seen the turning of your face, [O Muhammad], toward the heaven, and We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased. So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you [believers] are, turn your faces toward it [in prayer]. Indeed, those who have been given the Scripture well know that it is the truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do

2:145.ar: وَلَئِنۡ أَتَيۡتَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِكُلِّ ءَايَةࣲ مَّا تَبِعُواْ قِبۡلَتَكَۚ وَمَآ أَنتَ بِتَابِعࣲ قِبۡلَتَهُمۡۚ وَمَا بَعۡضُهُم بِتَابِعࣲ قِبۡلَةَ بَعۡضࣲۚ وَلَئِنِ ٱتَّبَعۡتَ أَهۡوَآءَهُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَكَ مِنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ إِنَّكَ إِذࣰ ا لَّمِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:145.en: And if you brought to those who were given the Scripture every sign, they would not follow your qiblah. Nor will you be a follower of their qiblah. Nor would they be followers of one another's qiblah. So if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, indeed, you would then be among the wrongdoers

2:146.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ يَعۡرِفُونَهُۥ كَمَا يَعۡرِفُونَ أَبۡنَآءَهُمۡۖ وَإِنَّ فَرِيقࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ لَيَكۡتُمُونَ ٱلۡحَقَّ وَهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُونَ
2:146.en: Those to whom We gave the Scripture know him as they know their own sons. But indeed, a party of them conceal the truth while they know [it]

2:147.ar: ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡمُمۡتَرِينَ
2:147.en: The truth is from your Lord, so never be among the doubters

2:148.ar: وَلِكُلࣲّ وِجۡهَةٌ هُوَ مُوَلِّيهَاۖ فَٱسۡتَبِقُواْ ٱلۡخَيۡرَٰتِۚ أَيۡنَ مَا تَكُونُواْ يَأۡتِ بِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ جَمِيعًاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
2:148.en: For each [religious following] is a direction toward which it faces. So race to [all that is] good. Wherever you may be, Allah will bring you forth [for judgement] all together. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent

2:149.ar: وَمِنۡ حَيۡثُ خَرَجۡتَ فَوَلِّ وَجۡهَكَ شَطۡرَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۖ وَإِنَّهُۥ لَلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَۗ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
2:149.en: So from wherever you go out [for prayer, O Muhammad] turn your face toward al- Masjid al-Haram, and indeed, it is the truth from your Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what you do

2:150.ar: وَمِنۡ حَيۡثُ خَرَجۡتَ فَوَلِّ وَجۡهَكَ شَطۡرَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۚ وَحَيۡثُ مَا كُنتُمۡ فَوَلُّواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ شَطۡرَهُۥ لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَيۡكُمۡ حُجَّةٌ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مِنۡهُمۡ فَلَا تَخۡشَوۡهُمۡ وَٱخۡشَوۡنِي وَلِأُتِمَّ نِعۡمَتِي عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَهۡتَدُونَ
2:150.en: And from wherever you go out [for prayer], turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you [believers] may be, turn your faces toward it in order that the people will not have any argument against you, except for those of them who commit wrong; so fear them not but fear Me. And [it is] so I may complete My favor upon you and that you may be guided

2:151.ar: كَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا فِيكُمۡ رَسُولࣰ ا مِّنكُمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا وَيُزَكِّيكُمۡ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَيُعَلِّمُكُم مَّا لَمۡ تَكُونُواْ تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:151.en: Just as We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves reciting to you Our verses and purifying you and teaching you the Book and wisdom and teaching you that which you did not know

2:152.ar: فَٱذۡكُرُونِيٓ أَذۡكُرۡكُمۡ وَٱشۡكُرُواْ لِي وَلَا تَكۡفُرُونِ
2:152.en: So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me

2:153.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱسۡتَعِينُواْ بِٱلصَّبۡرِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
2:153.en: O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient

2:154.ar: وَلَا تَقُولُواْ لِمَن يُقۡتَلُ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَمۡوَٰتُۢۚ بَلۡ أَحۡيَآءࣱ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تَشۡعُرُونَ
2:154.en: And do not say about those who are killed in the way of Allah, "They are dead." Rather, they are alive, but you perceive [it] not

2:155.ar: وَلَنَبۡلُوَنَّكُم بِشَيۡءࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡخَوۡفِ وَٱلۡجُوعِ وَنَقۡصࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَمۡوَٰلِ وَٱلۡأَنفُسِ وَٱلثَّمَرَٰتِۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
2:155.en: And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient

2:156.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَصَٰبَتۡهُم مُّصِيبَةࣱ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّآ إِلَيۡهِ رَٰجِعُونَ
2:156.en: Who, when disaster strikes them, say, "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return

2:157.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ صَلَوَٰتࣱ مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡ وَرَحۡمَةࣱۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُهۡتَدُونَ
2:157.en: Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy. And it is those who are the [rightly] guided

2:158.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱلصَّفَا وَٱلۡمَرۡوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَنۡ حَجَّ ٱلۡبَيۡتَ أَوِ ٱعۡتَمَرَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَاۚ وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرࣰ ا فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
2:158.en: Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever makes Hajj to the House or performs 'umrah - there is no blame upon him for walking between them. And whoever volunteers good - then indeed, Allah is appreciative and Knowing

2:159.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡتُمُونَ مَآ أَنزَلۡنَا مِنَ ٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ وَٱلۡهُدَىٰ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا بَيَّنَّٰهُ لِلنَّاسِ فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يَلۡعَنُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَيَلۡعَنُهُمُ ٱللَّٰعِنُونَ
2:159.en: Indeed, those who conceal what We sent down of clear proofs and guidance after We made it clear for the people in the Scripture - those are cursed by Allah and cursed by those who curse

2:160.ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ تَابُواْ وَأَصۡلَحُواْ وَبَيَّنُواْ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَتُوبُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَأَنَا ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:160.en: Except for those who repent and correct themselves and make evident [what they concealed]. Those - I will accept their repentance, and I am the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful

2:161.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَمَاتُواْ وَهُمۡ كُفَّارٌ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ لَعۡنَةُ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ أَجۡمَعِينَ
2:161.en: Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers - upon them will be the curse of Allah and of the angels and the people, all together

2:162.ar: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا لَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنۡهُمُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ وَلَا هُمۡ يُنظَرُونَ
2:162.en: Abiding eternally therein. The punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved

2:163.ar: وَإِلَٰهُكُمۡ إِلَٰهࣱ وَٰحِدࣱۖ لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:163.en: And your god is one God. There is no deity [worthy of worship] except Him, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful

2:164.ar: إِنَّ فِي خَلۡقِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱخۡتِلَٰفِ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ وَٱلۡفُلۡكِ ٱلَّتِي تَجۡرِي فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ بِمَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ وَمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مِن مَّآءࣲ فَأَحۡيَا بِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَا وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ دَآبَّةࣲ وَتَصۡرِيفِ ٱلرِّيَٰحِ وَٱلسَّحَابِ ٱلۡمُسَخَّرِ بَيۡنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡقِلُونَ
2:164.en: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the [great] ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people, and what Allah has sent down from the heavens of rain, giving life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness and dispersing therein every [kind of] moving creature, and [His] directing of the winds and the clouds controlled between the heaven and the earth are signs for a people who use reason

2:165.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَندَادࣰ ا يُحِبُّونَهُمۡ كَحُبِّ ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَشَدُّ حُبࣰّ ا لِّلَّهِۗ وَلَوۡ يَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ إِذۡ يَرَوۡنَ ٱلۡعَذَابَ أَنَّ ٱلۡقُوَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ
2:165.en: And [yet], among the people are those who take other than Allah as equals [to Him]. They love them as they [should] love Allah. But those who believe are stronger in love for Allah. And if only they who have wronged would consider [that] when they see the punishment, [they will be certain] that all power belongs to Allah and that Allah is severe in punishment

2:166.ar: إِذۡ تَبَرَّأَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتُّبِعُواْ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُواْ وَرَأَوُاْ ٱلۡعَذَابَ وَتَقَطَّعَتۡ بِهِمُ ٱلۡأَسۡبَابُ
2:166.en: [And they should consider that] when those who have been followed disassociate themselves from those who followed [them], and they [all] see the punishment, and cut off from them are the ties [of relationship]

2:167.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُواْ لَوۡ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةࣰ فَنَتَبَرَّأَ مِنۡهُمۡ كَمَا تَبَرَّءُواْ مِنَّاۗ كَذَٰلِكَ يُرِيهِمُ ٱللَّهُ أَعۡمَٰلَهُمۡ حَسَرَٰتٍ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ وَمَا هُم بِخَٰرِجِينَ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ
2:167.en: Those who followed will say, "If only we had another turn [at worldly life] so we could disassociate ourselves from them as they have disassociated themselves from us." Thus will Allah show them their deeds as regrets upon them. And they are never to emerge from the Fire

2:168.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ كُلُواْ مِمَّا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ حَلَٰلࣰ ا طَيِّبࣰ ا وَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ خُطُوَٰتِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَكُمۡ عَدُوࣱّ مُّبِينٌ
2:168.en: O mankind, eat from whatever is on earth [that is] lawful and good and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy

2:169.ar: إِنَّمَا يَأۡمُرُكُم بِٱلسُّوٓءِ وَٱلۡفَحۡشَآءِ وَأَن تَقُولُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:169.en: He only orders you to evil and immorality and to say about Allah what you do not know

2:170.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱتَّبِعُواْ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ قَالُواْ بَلۡ نَتَّبِعُ مَآ أَلۡفَيۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَنَآۚ أَوَلَوۡ كَانَ ءَابَآؤُهُمۡ لَا يَعۡقِلُونَ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يَهۡتَدُونَ
2:170.en: And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has revealed," they say, "Rather, we will follow that which we found our fathers doing." Even though their fathers understood nothing, nor were they guided

2:171.ar: وَمَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ كَمَثَلِ ٱلَّذِي يَنۡعِقُ بِمَا لَا يَسۡمَعُ إِلَّا دُعَآءࣰ وَنِدَآءࣰۚ صُمُّۢ بُكۡمٌ عُمۡيࣱ فَهُمۡ لَا يَعۡقِلُونَ
2:171.en: The example of those who disbelieve is like that of one who shouts at what hears nothing but calls and cries cattle or sheep - deaf, dumb and blind, so they do not understand

2:172.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُلُواْ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقۡنَٰكُمۡ وَٱشۡكُرُواْ لِلَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ إِيَّاهُ تَعۡبُدُونَ
2:172.en: O you who have believed, eat from the good things which We have provided for you and be grateful to Allah if it is [indeed] Him that you worship

2:173.ar: إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡمَيۡتَةَ وَٱلدَّمَ وَلَحۡمَ ٱلۡخِنزِيرِ وَمَآ أُهِلَّ بِهِۦ لِغَيۡرِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَنِ ٱضۡطُرَّ غَيۡرَ بَاغࣲ وَلَا عَادࣲ فَلَآ إِثۡمَ عَلَيۡهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
2:173.en: He has only forbidden to you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], there is no sin upon him. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful

2:174.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡتُمُونَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَيَشۡتَرُونَ بِهِۦ ثَمَنࣰ ا قَلِيلًا أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ مَا يَأۡكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمۡ إِلَّا ٱلنَّارَ وَلَا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَلَا يُزَكِّيهِمۡ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
2:174.en: Indeed, they who conceal what Allah has sent down of the Book and exchange it for a small price - those consume not into their bellies except the Fire. And Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them. And they will have a painful punishment

2:175.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱشۡتَرَوُاْ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةَ بِٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَٱلۡعَذَابَ بِٱلۡمَغۡفِرَةِۚ فَمَآ أَصۡبَرَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ
2:175.en: Those are the ones who have exchanged guidance for error and forgiveness for punishment. How patient they are in pursuit of the Fire

2:176.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ نَزَّلَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۗ وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَفِي شِقَاقِۭ بَعِيدࣲ‏
2:176.en: That is [deserved by them] because Allah has sent down the Book in truth. And indeed, those who differ over the Book are in extreme dissension

2:177.ar: ۞لَّيۡسَ ٱلۡبِرَّ أَن تُوَلُّواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ قِبَلَ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقِ وَٱلۡمَغۡرِبِ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلۡبِرَّ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ وَٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ وَءَاتَى ٱلۡمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِۦ ذَوِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينَ وَٱبۡنَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَٱلسَّآئِلِينَ وَفِي ٱلرِّقَابِ وَأَقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَى ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلۡمُوفُونَ بِعَهۡدِهِمۡ إِذَا عَٰهَدُواْۖ وَٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ فِي ٱلۡبَأۡسَآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ وَحِينَ ٱلۡبَأۡسِۗ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُواْۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُتَّقُونَ
2:177.en: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west, but [true] righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets and gives wealth, in spite of love for it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask [for help], and for freeing slaves; [and who] establishes prayer and gives zakah; [those who] fulfill their promise when they promise; and [those who] are patient in poverty and hardship and during battle. Those are the ones who have been true, and it is those who are the righteous

2:178.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡقِصَاصُ فِي ٱلۡقَتۡلَىۖ ٱلۡحُرُّ بِٱلۡحُرِّ وَٱلۡعَبۡدُ بِٱلۡعَبۡدِ وَٱلۡأُنثَىٰ بِٱلۡأُنثَىٰۚ فَمَنۡ عُفِيَ لَهُۥ مِنۡ أَخِيهِ شَيۡءࣱ فَٱتِّبَاعُۢ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَأَدَآءٌ إِلَيۡهِ بِإِحۡسَٰنࣲۗ ذَٰلِكَ تَخۡفِيفࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ وَرَحۡمَةࣱۗ فَمَنِ ٱعۡتَدَىٰ بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ فَلَهُۥ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
2:178.en: O you who have believed, prescribed for you is legal retribution for those murdered - the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female. But whoever overlooks from his brother anything, then there should be a suitable follow-up and payment to him with good conduct. This is an alleviation from your Lord and a mercy. But whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment

2:179.ar: وَلَكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡقِصَاصِ حَيَوٰةࣱ يَٰٓأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
2:179.en: And there is for you in legal retribution [saving of] life, O you [people] of understanding, that you may become righteous

2:180.ar: كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ إِن تَرَكَ خَيۡرًا ٱلۡوَصِيَّةُ لِلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبِينَ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِۖ حَقًّا عَلَى ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
2:180.en: Prescribed for you when death approaches [any] one of you if he leaves wealth [is that he should make] a bequest for the parents and near relatives according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the righteous

2:181.ar: فَمَنۢ بَدَّلَهُۥ بَعۡدَ مَا سَمِعَهُۥ فَإِنَّمَآ إِثۡمُهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُبَدِّلُونَهُۥٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمࣱ‏
2:181.en: Then whoever alters the bequest after he has heard it - the sin is only upon those who have altered it. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing

2:182.ar: فَمَنۡ خَافَ مِن مُّوصࣲ جَنَفًا أَوۡ إِثۡمࣰ ا فَأَصۡلَحَ بَيۡنَهُمۡ فَلَآ إِثۡمَ عَلَيۡهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
2:182.en: But if one fears from the bequeather [some] error or sin and corrects that which is between them, there is no sin upon him. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful

2:183.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
2:183.en: O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you that you may become righteous

2:184.ar: أَيَّامࣰ ا مَّعۡدُودَٰتࣲۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرࣲ فَعِدَّةࣱ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۚ وَعَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُۥ فِدۡيَةࣱ طَعَامُ مِسۡكِينࣲۖ فَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرࣰ ا فَهُوَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّهُۥۚ وَأَن تَصُومُواْ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:184.en: [Fasting for] a limited number of days. So whoever among you is ill or on a journey [during them] - then an equal number of days [are to be made up]. And upon those who are able [to fast, but with hardship] - a ransom [as substitute] of feeding a poor person [each day]. And whoever volunteers excess - it is better for him. But to fast is best for you, if you only knew

2:185.ar: شَهۡرُ رَمَضَانَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ هُدࣰ ى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَٱلۡفُرۡقَانِۚ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ ٱلشَّهۡرَ فَلۡيَصُمۡهُۖ وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرࣲ فَعِدَّةࣱ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۗ يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡيُسۡرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡعُسۡرَ وَلِتُكۡمِلُواْ ٱلۡعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
2:185.en: The month of Ramadhan [is that] in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for the people and clear proofs of guidance and criterion. So whoever sights [the new moon of] the month, let him fast it; and whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days. Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship and [wants] for you to complete the period and to glorify Allah for that [to] which He has guided you; and perhaps you will be grateful

2:186.ar: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌۖ أُجِيبُ دَعۡوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِۖ فَلۡيَسۡتَجِيبُواْ لِي وَلۡيُؤۡمِنُواْ بِي لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡشُدُونَ
2:186.en: And when My servants ask you, [O Muhammad], concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me [by obedience] and believe in Me that they may be [rightly] guided

2:187.ar: أُحِلَّ لَكُمۡ لَيۡلَةَ ٱلصِّيَامِ ٱلرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَآئِكُمۡۚ هُنَّ لِبَاسࣱ لَّكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ لِبَاسࣱ لَّهُنَّۗ عَلِمَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّكُمۡ كُنتُمۡ تَخۡتَانُونَ أَنفُسَكُمۡ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَعَفَا عَنكُمۡۖ فَٱلۡـَٰٔنَ بَٰشِرُوهُنَّ وَٱبۡتَغُواْ مَا كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۚ وَكُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡخَيۡطُ ٱلۡأَبۡيَضُ مِنَ ٱلۡخَيۡطِ ٱلۡأَسۡوَدِ مِنَ ٱلۡفَجۡرِۖ ثُمَّ أَتِمُّواْ ٱلصِّيَامَ إِلَى ٱلَّيۡلِۚ وَلَا تُبَٰشِرُوهُنَّ وَأَنتُمۡ عَٰكِفُونَ فِي ٱلۡمَسَٰجِدِۗ تِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا تَقۡرَبُوهَاۗ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَّقُونَ
2:187.en: It has been made permissible for you the night preceding fasting to go to your wives [for sexual relations]. They are clothing for you and you are clothing for them. Allah knows that you used to deceive yourselves, so He accepted your repentance and forgave you. So now, have relations with them and seek that which Allah has decreed for you. And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread [of night]. Then complete the fast until the sunset. And do not have relations with them as long as you are staying for worship in the mosques. These are the limits [set by] Allah, so do not approach them. Thus does Allah make clear His ordinances to the people that they may become righteous

2:188.ar: وَلَا تَأۡكُلُوٓاْ أَمۡوَٰلَكُم بَيۡنَكُم بِٱلۡبَٰطِلِ وَتُدۡلُواْ بِهَآ إِلَى ٱلۡحُكَّامِ لِتَأۡكُلُواْ فَرِيقࣰ ا مِّنۡ أَمۡوَٰلِ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَأَنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:188.en: And do not consume one another's wealth unjustly or send it [in bribery] to the rulers in order that [they might aid] you [to] consume a portion of the wealth of the people in sin, while you know [it is unlawful]

2:189.ar: ۞يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡأَهِلَّةِۖ قُلۡ هِيَ مَوَٰقِيتُ لِلنَّاسِ وَٱلۡحَجِّۗ وَلَيۡسَ ٱلۡبِرُّ بِأَن تَأۡتُواْ ٱلۡبُيُوتَ مِن ظُهُورِهَا وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلۡبِرَّ مَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰۗ وَأۡتُواْ ٱلۡبُيُوتَ مِنۡ أَبۡوَٰبِهَاۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
2:189.en: They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the new moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people and for Hajj." And it is not righteousness to enter houses from the back, but righteousness is [in] one who fears Allah. And enter houses from their doors. And fear Allah that you may succeed

2:190.ar: وَقَٰتِلُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِينَ يُقَٰتِلُونَكُمۡ وَلَا تَعۡتَدُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُعۡتَدِينَ
2:190.en: Fight in the way of Allah those who fight you but do not transgress. Indeed. Allah does not like transgressors

2:191.ar: وَٱقۡتُلُوهُمۡ حَيۡثُ ثَقِفۡتُمُوهُمۡ وَأَخۡرِجُوهُم مِّنۡ حَيۡثُ أَخۡرَجُوكُمۡۚ وَٱلۡفِتۡنَةُ أَشَدُّ مِنَ ٱلۡقَتۡلِۚ وَلَا تُقَٰتِلُوهُمۡ عِندَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ حَتَّىٰ يُقَٰتِلُوكُمۡ فِيهِۖ فَإِن قَٰتَلُوكُمۡ فَٱقۡتُلُوهُمۡۗ كَذَٰلِكَ جَزَآءُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:191.en: And kill them wherever you overtake them and expel them from wherever they have expelled you, and fitnah is worse than killing. And do not fight them at al-Masjid al- Haram until they fight you there. But if they fight you, then kill them. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers

2:192.ar: فَإِنِ ٱنتَهَوۡاْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
2:192.en: And if they cease, then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful

2:193.ar: وَقَٰتِلُوهُمۡ حَتَّىٰ لَا تَكُونَ فِتۡنَةࣱ وَيَكُونَ ٱلدِّينُ لِلَّهِۖ فَإِنِ ٱنتَهَوۡاْ فَلَا عُدۡوَٰنَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:193.en: Fight them until there is no [more] fitnah and [until] worship is [acknowledged to be] for Allah. But if they cease, then there is to be no aggression except against the oppressors

2:194.ar: ٱلشَّهۡرُ ٱلۡحَرَامُ بِٱلشَّهۡرِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ وَٱلۡحُرُمَٰتُ قِصَاصࣱۚ فَمَنِ ٱعۡتَدَىٰ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فَٱعۡتَدُواْ عَلَيۡهِ بِمِثۡلِ مَا ٱعۡتَدَىٰ عَلَيۡكُمۡۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
2:194.en: [Fighting in] the sacred month is for [aggression committed in] the sacred month, and for [all] violations is legal retribution. So whoever has assaulted you, then assault him in the same way that he has assaulted you. And fear Allah and know that Allah is with those who fear Him

2:195.ar: وَأَنفِقُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا تُلۡقُواْ بِأَيۡدِيكُمۡ إِلَى ٱلتَّهۡلُكَةِ وَأَحۡسِنُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
2:195.en: And spend in the way of Allah and do not throw [yourselves] with your [own] hands into destruction [by refraining]. And do good; indeed, Allah loves the doers of good

2:196.ar: وَأَتِمُّواْ ٱلۡحَجَّ وَٱلۡعُمۡرَةَ لِلَّهِۚ فَإِنۡ أُحۡصِرۡتُمۡ فَمَا ٱسۡتَيۡسَرَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَدۡيِۖ وَلَا تَحۡلِقُواْ رُءُوسَكُمۡ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡلُغَ ٱلۡهَدۡيُ مَحِلَّهُۥۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ بِهِۦٓ أَذࣰ ى مِّن رَّأۡسِهِۦ فَفِدۡيَةࣱ مِّن صِيَامٍ أَوۡ صَدَقَةٍ أَوۡ نُسُكࣲۚ فَإِذَآ أَمِنتُمۡ فَمَن تَمَتَّعَ بِٱلۡعُمۡرَةِ إِلَى ٱلۡحَجِّ فَمَا ٱسۡتَيۡسَرَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَدۡيِۚ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامࣲ فِي ٱلۡحَجِّ وَسَبۡعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعۡتُمۡۗ تِلۡكَ عَشَرَةࣱ كَامِلَةࣱۗ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن لَّمۡ يَكُنۡ أَهۡلُهُۥ حَاضِرِي ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
2:196.en: And complete the Hajj and 'umrah for Allah. But if you are prevented, then [offer] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal has reached its place of slaughter. And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head [making shaving necessary must offer] a ransom of fasting [three days] or charity or sacrifice. And when you are secure, then whoever performs 'umrah [during the Hajj months] followed by Hajj [offers] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And whoever cannot find [or afford such an animal] - then a fast of three days during Hajj and of seven when you have returned [home]. Those are ten complete [days]. This is for those whose family is not in the area of al-Masjid al-Haram. And fear Allah and know that Allah is severe in penalty

2:197.ar: ٱلۡحَجُّ أَشۡهُرࣱ مَّعۡلُومَٰتࣱۚ فَمَن فَرَضَ فِيهِنَّ ٱلۡحَجَّ فَلَا رَفَثَ وَلَا فُسُوقَ وَلَا جِدَالَ فِي ٱلۡحَجِّۗ وَمَا تَفۡعَلُواْ مِنۡ خَيۡرࣲ يَعۡلَمۡهُ ٱللَّهُۗ وَتَزَوَّدُواْ فَإِنَّ خَيۡرَ ٱلزَّادِ ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰۖ وَٱتَّقُونِ يَٰٓأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
2:197.en: Hajj is [during] well-known months, so whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon himself therein [by entering the state of ihram], there is [to be for him] no sexual relations and no disobedience and no disputing during Hajj. And whatever good you do - Allah knows it. And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of Allah. And fear Me, O you of understanding

2:198.ar: لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَبۡتَغُواْ فَضۡلࣰ ا مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡۚ فَإِذَآ أَفَضۡتُم مِّنۡ عَرَفَٰتࣲ فَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عِندَ ٱلۡمَشۡعَرِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۖ وَٱذۡكُرُوهُ كَمَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَإِن كُنتُم مِّن قَبۡلِهِۦ لَمِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
2:198.en: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord [during Hajj]. But when you depart from 'Arafat, remember Allah at al- Mash'ar al-Haram. And remember Him, as He has guided you, for indeed, you were before that among those astray

2:199.ar: ثُمَّ أَفِيضُواْ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ أَفَاضَ ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
2:199.en: Then depart from the place from where [all] the people depart and ask forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful

2:200.ar: فَإِذَا قَضَيۡتُم مَّنَٰسِكَكُمۡ فَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ كَذِكۡرِكُمۡ ءَابَآءَكُمۡ أَوۡ أَشَدَّ ذِكۡرࣰ اۗ فَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَمَا لَهُۥ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ مِنۡ خَلَٰقࣲ‏
2:200.en: And when you have completed your rites, remember Allah like your [previous] remembrance of your fathers or with [much] greater remembrance. And among the people is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world," and he will have in the Hereafter no share

2:201.ar: وَمِنۡهُم مَّن يَقُولُ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا حَسَنَةࣰ وَفِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ حَسَنَةࣰ وَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ
2:201.en: But among them is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter [that which is] good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire

2:202.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمۡ نَصِيبࣱ مِّمَّا كَسَبُواْۚ وَٱللَّهُ سَرِيعُ ٱلۡحِسَابِ
2:202.en: Those will have a share of what they have earned, and Allah is swift in account

2:219.ar: ۞يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡخَمۡرِ وَٱلۡمَيۡسِرِۖ قُلۡ فِيهِمَآ إِثۡمࣱ كَبِيرࣱ وَمَنَٰفِعُ لِلنَّاسِ وَإِثۡمُهُمَآ أَكۡبَرُ مِن نَّفۡعِهِمَاۗ وَيَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنفِقُونَۖ قُلِ ٱلۡعَفۡوَۗ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ
2:219.en: They ask you about wine and gambling. Say, "In them is great sin and [yet, some] benefit for people. But their sin is greater than their benefit." And they ask you what they should spend. Say, "The excess [beyond needs]." Thus Allah makes clear to you the verses [of revelation] that you might give thought

2:220.ar: فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۗ وَيَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰۖ قُلۡ إِصۡلَاحࣱ لَّهُمۡ خَيۡرࣱۖ وَإِن تُخَالِطُوهُمۡ فَإِخۡوَٰنُكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُصۡلِحِۚ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَأَعۡنَتَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
2:220.en: To this world and the Hereafter. And they ask you about orphans. Say, "Improvement for them is best. And if you mix your affairs with theirs - they are your brothers. And Allah knows the corrupter from the amender. And if Allah had willed, He could have put you in difficulty. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise

2:221.ar: وَلَا تَنكِحُواْ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكَٰتِ حَتَّىٰ يُؤۡمِنَّۚ وَلَأَمَةࣱ مُّؤۡمِنَةٌ خَيۡرࣱ مِّن مُّشۡرِكَةࣲ وَلَوۡ أَعۡجَبَتۡكُمۡۗ وَلَا تُنكِحُواْ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ حَتَّىٰ يُؤۡمِنُواْۚ وَلَعَبۡدࣱ مُّؤۡمِنٌ خَيۡرࣱ مِّن مُّشۡرِكࣲ وَلَوۡ أَعۡجَبَكُمۡۗ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يَدۡعُونَ إِلَى ٱلنَّارِۖ وَٱللَّهُ يَدۡعُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱلۡجَنَّةِ وَٱلۡمَغۡفِرَةِ بِإِذۡنِهِۦۖ وَيُبَيِّنُ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ
2:221.en: And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe. And a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist, even though she might please you. And do not marry polytheistic men [to your women] until they believe. And a believing slave is better than a polytheist, even though he might please you. Those invite [you] to the Fire, but Allah invites to Paradise and to forgiveness, by His permission. And He makes clear His verses to the people that perhaps they may remember

2:223.ar: نِسَآؤُكُمۡ حَرۡثࣱ لَّكُمۡ فَأۡتُواْ حَرۡثَكُمۡ أَنَّىٰ شِئۡتُمۡۖ وَقَدِّمُواْ لِأَنفُسِكُمۡۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّكُم مُّلَٰقُوهُۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
2:223.en: Your wives are a place of sowing of seed for you, so come to your place of cultivation however you wish and put forth [righteousness] for yourselves. And fear Allah and know that you will meet Him. And give good tidings to the believers

2:227.ar: وَإِنۡ عَزَمُواْ ٱلطَّلَٰقَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمࣱ‏
2:227.en: And if they decide on divorce - then indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing

2:229.ar: ٱلطَّلَٰقُ مَرَّتَانِۖ فَإِمۡسَاكُۢ بِمَعۡرُوفٍ أَوۡ تَسۡرِيحُۢ بِإِحۡسَٰنࣲۗ وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمۡ أَن تَأۡخُذُواْ مِمَّآ ءَاتَيۡتُمُوهُنَّ شَيۡـًٔا إِلَّآ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِۖ فَإِنۡ خِفۡتُمۡ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِمَا فِيمَا ٱفۡتَدَتۡ بِهِۦۗ تِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا تَعۡتَدُوهَاۚ وَمَن يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
2:229.en: Divorce is twice. Then, either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment. And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them unless both fear that they will not be able to keep [within] the limits of Allah. But if you fear that they will not keep [within] the limits of Allah, then there is no blame upon either of them concerning that by which she ransoms herself. These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah - it is those who are the wrongdoers

2:230.ar: فَإِن طَلَّقَهَا فَلَا تَحِلُّ لَهُۥ مِنۢ بَعۡدُ حَتَّىٰ تَنكِحَ زَوۡجًا غَيۡرَهُۥۗ فَإِن طَلَّقَهَا فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِمَآ أَن يَتَرَاجَعَآ إِن ظَنَّآ أَن يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِۗ وَتِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ يُبَيِّنُهَا لِقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡلَمُونَ
2:230.en: And if he has divorced her [for the third time], then she is not lawful to him afterward until [after] she marries a husband other than him. And if the latter husband divorces her [or dies], there is no blame upon the woman and her former husband for returning to each other if they think that they can keep [within] the limits of Allah. These are the limits of Allah, which He makes clear to a people who know

2:231.ar: وَإِذَا طَلَّقۡتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَبَلَغۡنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَأَمۡسِكُوهُنَّ بِمَعۡرُوفٍ أَوۡ سَرِّحُوهُنَّ بِمَعۡرُوفࣲۚ وَلَا تُمۡسِكُوهُنَّ ضِرَارࣰ ا لِّتَعۡتَدُواْۚ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡ ذَٰلِكَ فَقَدۡ ظَلَمَ نَفۡسَهُۥۚ وَلَا تَتَّخِذُوٓاْ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ هُزُوࣰ اۚ وَٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَمَآ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةِ يَعِظُكُم بِهِۦۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣱ‏
2:231.en: And when you divorce women and they have [nearly] fulfilled their term, either retain them according to acceptable terms or release them according to acceptable terms, and do not keep them, intending harm, to transgress [against them]. And whoever does that has certainly wronged himself. And do not take the verses of Allah in jest. And remember the favor of Allah upon you and what has been revealed to you of the Book and wisdom by which He instructs you. And fear Allah and know that Allah is Knowing of all things

2:238.ar: حَٰفِظُواْ عَلَى ٱلصَّلَوَٰتِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِ ٱلۡوُسۡطَىٰ وَقُومُواْ لِلَّهِ قَٰنِتِينَ
2:238.en: Maintain with care the [obligatory] prayers and [in particular] the middle prayer and stand before Allah, devoutly obedient

8iO4fUKblrk.speaker: adnan
8iO4fUKblrk.speaker_note: hosts his own A Juz A Day Ramadan series; single voice throughout
8iO4fUKblrk.title: A Juz A Day: 2nd Juz, Our Turn to Lead
8iO4fUKblrk.one_line: After the Israelites' compromised leadership and Ibrahim's model, the change of qiblah hands leadership to this ummah, and the Sharia of Al-Baqarah shows how to carry it.
8iO4fUKblrk.summary: He frames the second juz as a transfer of leadership. The Israelites were favoured and given leadership but kept bargaining it down, while Ibrahim earned his after passing every test and was told leadership is not inherited by wrongdoing descendants. Building the Kaaba in old age and asking only for acceptance shows the attitude of the righteous, and Ibrahim's prayer for a messenger defines four tasks of real Islamic education: recitation, scripture, wisdom and purification. The change of qiblah then marks the changing of the guard; he argues that wasat means the best community, meant to lead by example rather than accept being downtrodden. He then surveys the Sharia as the content of that leadership: the truly guided are those who stay calm and keep working under trial; studying creation should end in love for the Creator; eating halal should end in gratitude; haram is a short defined list and necessity lifts it; piety is iman producing hard action, not ritual alone. He covers retribution as deterrence, fasting with its purpose stated before its rulings, Ramadan and dua, weighing harm against benefit with alcohol and gambling, protecting orphans' wealth, marrying someone who shares your worldview, and justice in divorce. He asks the ummah to lead through character and morality.

outline.heading: Opening
The Israelites' compromised leadership
outline.gist: They were favoured and given leadership with expectations, but took shortcuts, made excuses and tried to shrink the burden; this is presented as a warning to the reader.

outline.heading: Ibrahim: tested first, then made a leader
outline.gist: Leadership came only after Ibrahim fulfilled every test; when he asked for his descendants, Allah said the pledge does not reach wrongdoers, so leadership is earned by action and sacrifice, not genetics.

outline.heading: Building the Kaaba and asking only for acceptance
outline.gist: In old age and desert heat Ibrahim and Ismail raise the House and ask only that Allah accept it; the righteous seek no recognition and make no complaint.

outline.heading: Make us and our descendants devoted to You
outline.gist: Ibrahim prays that he and his offspring be a community submitted to Allah, shown how to worship and forgiven.

outline.heading: The Prophet's four duties as the answer to Ibrahim's prayer
outline.gist: Reciting revelation, teaching scripture, teaching wisdom (the Sunnah) and purifying souls; Islamic education that misses any of these is not being done correctly.

outline.heading: Who but a fool forsakes the way of Ibrahim
outline.gist: A pointed challenge to all who claim Abrahamic faith to return to Ibrahim's actual way.

outline.heading: The change of qiblah: now it is our turn to lead
outline.gist: After the Israelites and Ibrahim, Allah turns to this ummah; the point of the qiblah change is following Allah's command, not the direction itself.

outline.heading: Context of the qiblah change and the mockery in Madinah
outline.gist: Praying toward Jerusalem put the Kaaba behind them in Madinah for 16 to 18 months; the Prophet longed for the Kaaba, and when it changed some in Madinah used it to ridicule and sow doubt, which weighed on the believers.

outline.heading: Your prayers were never wasted
outline.gist: Companions worried their earlier prayers were invalid; Allah calls those prayers iman and promises they will not be lost, while the House Ibrahim built becomes the ummah's direction.

outline.heading: Ummatan wasata means the best community
outline.gist: Wasat in Arabic usage means the best, not merely balanced; the ummah is meant to lead by example and should not accept being downtrodden as normal.

outline.heading: The Sharia as the content of leadership
outline.gist: Leadership is not a title but a comprehensive way of life: spirituality, contemplation, halal consumption, justice, fasting, sacrifice, Hajj, morality and family.

outline.heading: Tests of fear and loss build resilience
outline.gist: Allah promises trials and tells believers to seek help in patience and prayer; each test endured with trust upgrades patience and builds strong, resilient character.

outline.heading: Only those who stay patient are truly guided
outline.gist: The verse restricts guidance to those who say they belong to Allah and return to Him; this is a test to judge ourselves by, not others.

outline.heading: Signs in creation for those who use their minds
outline.gist: The heavens and earth, night and day, ships, rain, creatures, winds and clouds are signs for people of reason.

outline.heading: The believers' most intense love is for Allah
outline.gist: People may love many things, but the believer's highest love is Allah and His Messenger, unlike those who love rivals as Allah should be loved.

outline.heading: Studying nature should end in love of the Creator
outline.gist: Science and the study of systems are part of the deen; the Muslim reaches the same findings as anyone but they culminate in appreciation and love of Allah, pondering the verses in the book and outside it.

outline.heading: Eat what is good and be grateful
outline.gist: Eating good, lawful food and not following Satan's footsteps; consumption that ends in gratitude becomes worship.

outline.heading: Haram is defined, everything else is halal
outline.gist: The restrictive wording of the verse shows that forbidden foods are a short list, extended slightly by the Sunnah, with permissibility as the default.

outline.heading: Necessity lifts the prohibition
outline.gist: Whoever is forced by hunger, not desire or excess, commits no sin; survival allows the haram.

outline.heading: Piety is more than ritual
outline.gist: Before the ritual rulings arrive, Allah says righteousness is not facing east or west; rituals are part of piety but not all of it.

outline.heading: Iman that produces costly giving
outline.gist: True righteousness starts with belief and produces giving of cherished wealth to a wide range of causes, trusting Allah to replace it.

outline.heading: Prayer, zakat and keeping your word
outline.gist: Keeping promises is part of iman; making promises and breaking them is unacceptable in Islam.

outline.heading: Steadfast in adversity: iman as the engine
outline.gist: Composure in danger grows out of iman; the Quran focuses on building iman because it drives all action, while the Sunnah details the how.

outline.heading: Retribution as a source of life
outline.gist: Qisas is applied to a small minority after due process and deters the rest, which is why the verse calls it life; critics of the penal code miss this objective.

outline.heading: Rulings of fasting and its concessions
outline.gist: Fasting is prescribed for taqwa; the ill and travellers make up days, while the very old or chronically ill feed a needy person instead.

outline.heading: The why before the how
outline.gist: Allah states the purpose of fasting before its rulings, a pattern across the Quran, because once the why is clear the how follows.

outline.heading: Ramadan, the month of the Quran
outline.gist: The only mention of Ramadan in the Quran is tied to the Quran; studying it strengthens iman, which makes fasting more fruitful, a feedback loop.

outline.heading: I am near: a time for dua
outline.gist: Responding to Allah means asking Him, and asking is itself an expression of iman that leads to guidance; dua is the essence of worship.

outline.heading: Spouses as garments: do not neglect family in Ramadan
outline.gist: Husband and wife are close, protective and beautifying like garments; worship in Ramadan should not crowd out the marriage.

outline.heading: Fighting within limits
outline.gist: Fighting is the work of an organized state army, mainly defensive, and limits must never be overstepped even in battle.

outline.heading: Objective morality and principles for new questions
outline.gist: The Quran gives an authoritative basis for good and evil and also principles to judge matters it does not name.

outline.heading: Alcohol and gambling: harm outweighs benefit
outline.gist: The Quran admits some benefit, such as lottery-funded causes, but most gamblers lose in a zero-sum game; weighing harm against benefit explains why something is forbidden.

outline.heading: Hajj: the best provision is taqwa
outline.gist: Returning to the skipped Hajj passage: preparing for the journey starts with consciousness of Allah.

outline.heading: Good in this life and the next
outline.gist: Some ask only for this world and get only that; others ask for good in both and protection from the Fire, the Prophet's most frequent dua.

outline.heading: Protecting the orphan's wealth
outline.gist: Orphans are easy to exploit through their inheritance; mixing their affairs with yours is allowed but they are your brothers and Allah knows who corrupts and who improves.

outline.heading: Marry someone who shares your worldview
outline.gist: Marriage to idol worshippers is forbidden because a spouse without the same moral basis forces a choice between principles and partner.

outline.heading: Procreation and legacy as an objective of marriage
outline.gist: The field metaphor describes conception; alongside companionship and tranquillity, raising faithful children carries one's legacy forward.

outline.heading: Justice even when deciding to divorce
outline.gist: Allah hears and knows; justice must hold in an emotionally charged time.

outline.heading: Divorce in stages keeps reconciliation open
outline.gist: The two revocable divorces exist so the door to reconciliation stays open; using them to harm a wife is haram and makes a mockery of revelation.

outline.heading: Guard the prayers amid hardship; lead by example
outline.gist: Placed in the middle of the divorce passage, the command to guard prayers is Allah's advice in stress; the juz ties back to leading with justice, compassion and resilience.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: The purposes behind Allah's commands (maqasid)

themes.note: Piety starts with iman, which produces costly giving, kept promises and composure; the Quran focuses on building it.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it

themes.note: Objective morality from revelation plus the principle of weighing harm against benefit.

themes.note: Orphans' rights, choosing a spouse, procreation as legacy and justice in divorce.

2:185.ar: شَهۡرُ رَمَضَانَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ هُدࣰ ى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَٱلۡفُرۡقَانِۚ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ ٱلشَّهۡرَ فَلۡيَصُمۡهُۖ وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرࣲ فَعِدَّةࣱ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۗ يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡيُسۡرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡعُسۡرَ وَلِتُكۡمِلُواْ ٱلۡعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
2:185.en: The month of Ramadhan [is that] in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for the people and clear proofs of guidance and criterion. FdLkq6W99Dw.title: A Plan for Ramadan
FdLkq6W99Dw.one_line: A ten-point plan for Ramadan: intention, fasting with excellence, Quran, dhikr, prayer, knowledge, relationships, service, dua, and planning your life.
FdLkq6W99Dw.summary: Respecting an opportunity means planning for it, and Ramadan never arrives by surprise. After the hadith in which the Prophet describes Ramadan as a month of blessing in which Allah watches His servants compete and boasts of them to the angels, he lays out ten points to write down. First, set a clear and sincere intention, since people themselves judge deeds by their motives, and aim for this to be your best Ramadan ever. Second, fast with excellence: fasting is not a handicap but proof of how little you need, a step further from the forbidden, and a training of the self that should extend to the tongue, eyes, ears and hands. Third, enjoy the Quran through a daily portion that is never skipped and a few verses kept for reflection, since Ramadan is the annual Quran retreat. Fourth, build daily dhikr in place of irritation, chatter and scrolling. Fifth, invest in prayer, with the young standing the full taraweeh. Then commit to daily learning, repair broken relationships, serve others, learn dua as an art and write your duas down, and use the quiet of fasting to plan your life's direction, even though the plans themselves will change.

outline.heading: Opening
The companions anchored their year on Ramadan
outline.gist: They spent months asking to reach Ramadan and months asking for its acceptance; even people far from Allah find closeness when He opens the gates of Paradise.

outline.heading: Respecting an opportunity means planning for it
outline.gist: Ramadan never comes as a surprise, so plan well; he has already booked off the last ten nights of next year's Ramadan.

outline.heading: A month of barakah: the smallest deed amplified
outline.gist: In the hadith of the blessed month, barakah means Allah turning something small into something far greater, as He made everything from nothing.

outline.heading: Competing to lift each other and Allah boasting of His servants
outline.gist: Allah sends mercy, removes sins and accepts dua, then watches people compete to motivate one another and shows them off to the angels who doubted humanity; so show Him your best.

outline.heading: Point one: deeds are only as good as their intention
outline.gist: Even outside religion people feel betrayed when they learn a kind act had another motive, and marriages and friendships end over it; Allah too judges actions by what they aimed at.

outline.heading: Ask why you fast and pray; write your goals
outline.gist: Decide now what you want from the month, from closeness to Allah to changing habits or companions, so you can keep checking whether you have reached it.

outline.heading: Intend this to be your best Ramadan
outline.gist: Keep standing goals plus one specific to this year; the moment you look back on an earlier Ramadan as your best, you have started going backwards.

outline.heading: Point two: fasting is not a handicap
outline.gist: Treating the fast as an excuse to be tired, unproductive or irritable turns it into a handicap; it shows how little you need and removes the constant distraction of food.

outline.heading: One step further from haram; taming the self
outline.gist: Giving up the lawful puts you further from the forbidden, so scrolling or gossiping while fasting makes no sense; Allah has no need for the hunger of someone who keeps lying.

outline.heading: If you can skip the midday tea, you can do anything
outline.gist: Not making a cup of tea after his morning clinic proves to him that the self can be tamed from temper, gossip and arrogance too.

outline.heading: Fasting with every limb, in your own context
outline.gist: Withhold the tongue, eyes, ears, hands and feet from sin; for him excellence means giving patients full attention and being present with his children without complaining.

outline.heading: Point three: enjoy the Quran
outline.gist: Everything about the Quran is beautiful, artistic, intellectual and emotional, and it serves the simplest and most complex minds alike; it saved us before and will again.

outline.heading: A daily portion you never skip
outline.gist: The Prophet told those who missed their nightly portion to make it up in the morning; pick an amount you can keep, a juz or a page, and carry it beyond Ramadan.

outline.heading: Scholars who set hadith aside for the Quran
outline.gist: He was taught to do nothing in Ramadan but read Quran, as great hadith scholars, including Imam Malik, closed their classes for the month and devoted themselves to it.

outline.heading: Recite continuously and contemplate a few verses
outline.gist: He keeps reading without counting khatmas, while spending weeks on a few verses or a surah, reading and listening to what scholars say about them.

outline.heading: Ramadan's status comes from the Quran
outline.gist: The month is honoured because the Quran was revealed in it, so focusing on the Quran is focusing on its reason; Ramadan is our annual Quran retreat.

outline.heading: Point four: dhikr instead of venting or scrolling
outline.gist: When fasting makes you want to snap, turn to remembrance; there is no halal scrolling, only meaningless clips or worse.

outline.heading: Start small and build a daily wird
outline.gist: The Prophet taught a daily portion of Quran and dhikr; one of his teachers built over fifty years from a hundred to ten thousand salawat a day.

outline.heading: Simple numbers that add up
outline.gist: Three hundred on the way to work and back, a hundred after each prayer and before sleep quickly passes a thousand with little effort.

outline.heading: Dhikr instead of chatter before prayer
outline.gist: Sit in remembrance during the talk before Isha instead of chatting, so the heart calms; the Prophet's one thing to hold onto was a tongue moist with remembrance.

outline.heading: Point five: invest in your prayer
outline.gist: Around four hundred rakat of taraweeh in a month is practice for finding the heart in prayer, so that afterward prayer is rest rather than a burden.

outline.heading: Young people: never leave taraweeh early
outline.gist: He forbids young men from skipping or leaving taraweeh early while their knees work and they have time; those who leave do not sleep earlier anyway.

outline.heading: Standing beside the Ka'bah as a boy
outline.gist: His father worked at the Zamzam pumps and left him in the Haram, where he squeezed in by the rail and prayed the full taraweeh, his best memories to this day.

outline.heading: Pray every prayer in congregation, even at home
outline.gist: Do not miss a daily prayer, pray in congregation as often as possible, with a roommate or relative if not at the masjid, and listen to the whole Quran in prayer.

outline.heading: Point six: commit to a daily lesson
outline.gist: Ramadan is when scholars release their best series; find someone you connect with and learn something every day.

outline.heading: The mind works best on an empty stomach
outline.gist: Memorization doubled or tripled in Ramadan; as a child he memorized a whole juz in one day, page by page.

outline.heading: Point seven: revive severed relationships
outline.gist: Fix ties with parents, relatives and estranged friends at the start of the month for your own clean heart, and call someone you have neglected for years each day.

outline.heading: Point eight: be of service
outline.gist: With the right intention, volunteering earns the reward of the prayer you missed as well as the service; give, teach, or help however you can.

outline.heading: Teaching his brother Quran at fifteen
outline.gist: He taught his youngest brother and two cousins, finished with them in Ramadan with gifts and a celebration none of them forgot; teenagers should find a child to teach.

outline.heading: Badr was in Ramadan: a month of action
outline.gist: Many decisive events in Islamic history fell in Ramadan; it is not a month to sit at home but to serve.

outline.heading: Point nine: dua is an art
outline.gist: Speaking to the King of kings differs from speaking to any creature; in dua you lay out fears, hopes and the emotions you wish you had or did not have, with hands raised as the Prophet did.

outline.heading: Write down your duas for sujud
outline.gist: Write and memorize the duas you will make in every prostration of the month and keep building this conversation.

outline.heading: Point ten: worship by planning your life
outline.gist: Use the month to ask what you will do with your few laps around the sun and what your legacy will be; planning shows what you care about even if the plan fails.

outline.heading: What is your role in the victory you pray for?
outline.gist: When praying for the ummah's success, think about the steps it requires, your role in them, and make dua for your first step.

outline.heading: The notebooks he carried out of Syria
outline.gist: Fleeing at night, he packed his planning notebooks instead of clothes; none of his milestones happened, but planning gave him a direction toward Allah that held.

outline.heading: Recap of the ten-point plan
outline.gist: He runs back through all ten points, adding that being of service is the way out of selfishness and that dua answers the Quran in which Allah spoke first.

outline.heading: Outro

i0gqagJ2xas.speaker_note: Opens his own Ramadan 2026 post-Fajr series on the values of Islam; mentions his 25 years of study
i0gqagJ2xas.title: The Values of Islam: Introduction to Values, Principles and Ethics
i0gqagJ2xas.one_line: Defines values, principles and ethics, and argues that Islam's real gift is the correct ranking of values, which the ummah has lost.
i0gqagJ2xas.summary: Opening his Ramadan series, he separates three ideas that people blur. A value answers what rule you live by; a principle is how you behave because of it; ethics is judging whether following one rule violates a superior one. Everyone has values, even the worst people, but being ethical means ranking them correctly. A man who cheats to provide for his family has values but no ethics. The Quran shows this ranking: parents are obeyed second only to Allah, but never into shirk, and one must testify truthfully even against parents. Fiqh rulings change with every new fatwa, yet the core values are not disputed; people simply take from Islam what fits their assumptions and justify their choices. The Prophet was sent to perfect noble character, making the order of values clear so that no one could justify harm or oppression through a value. Tempters want a principled person to slip just once, which is why Quraysh, finding no ethical fault in the Prophet, could only call him mad. He urges parents to teach children ethics, not just ritual, and closes with an image of the Prophet's carefully ordered stack of values dropped and restacked wrongly somewhere in history.

outline.heading: Rulings differ by school, values do not
outline.gist: Schools of law differ on details such as dogs, but nobody differs on eating unlawful wealth; that belongs to values, principles and ethics.

outline.heading: Three questions: values, principles, ethics
outline.gist: A value is the rule you live by, a principle is how you behave given that rule, and ethics asks whether following it violates a superior rule. The breakdown draws on Kant's Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals and The Elements of Moral Philosophy.

outline.heading: The Quran's words for value and character
outline.gist: The Quran speaks of a value-based religion and of the Prophet's tremendous character; his character being the Quran means he judged which principle to follow by the Quran.

outline.heading: Loyalty: everyone has values
outline.gist: Loyalty becomes the principle of protecting colleagues, but will you lie for one who harms someone? Everyone has values in a subconscious black box; the question is whether they have ethics.

outline.heading: Ethics is the ranking of values
outline.gist: A man who earns unlawful money because he takes care of his family has a value but is unethical; ethics means knowing which principles may be overridden by which values.

outline.heading: Starting with values never to be violated
outline.gist: The series begins with the values that can never be broken, because without an ethical system a person can pick a beautiful value from the Quran and misuse it.

outline.heading: Parents: obeyed after Allah, but not into disobedience
outline.gist: Kindness to parents is ranked right after worshipping Allah, yet if they push you to shirk you do not obey; no creature is obeyed in disobedience to the Creator.

outline.heading: Truthful testimony even against parents
outline.gist: Loyalty to family yields to justice: the Quran commands truthful testimony even against one's parents, one of its hardest and most ethical verses, and no contradiction.

outline.heading: People take from Islam what fits their assumptions
outline.gist: Years of asking people what Islam stands for produced scattered answers; the companions, by contrast, had the values, principles and ranking embedded in them.

outline.heading: Rulings change, values stay constant
outline.gist: New fatwas appear every year and that is fine, but the values are agreed upon; the difference is that some people hold to their ethical system and others find a way around it and justify themselves.

outline.heading: Sent to perfect noble character
outline.gist: A value has to turn into a verb, such as honesty into telling the truth. The Prophet was sent to complete good character so the ranking would be clear and no one could justify harm or oppression through a value.

outline.heading: One misplaced value ruins a person
outline.gist: Even the most evil people have values; putting one value above another in the wrong order makes someone untrustworthy and harmful, and the ummah today justifies itself this way.

outline.heading: Interlude
The values are familiar; the question is their place
outline.gist: None of the values will be new; what matters is where each fits in the order all the prophets brought, which people know deep down.

outline.heading: Seeking a free pass from the imam
outline.gist: Fiqh questions are easy; ethical ones depend on what the asker reveals. People know when they are breaching a principle because Allah placed that sense in them, and revelation made the list firm.

outline.heading: Tempted to sell out just once
outline.gist: The Quran's stories show people pressured to compromise their ethics who refused; those already compromised only want you to do it once.

outline.heading: They would almost make you slip with their eyes
outline.gist: People like to see the ethical fall because it comforts their own breaches. Unable to find any ethical fault in the Prophet, his enemies could only call him mad, which is not an ethical charge.

outline.heading: Interlude
Teach children ethics, not only ritual
outline.gist: The series is meant as a resource for parents; wudu and prayer matter, but a child without values, principles and ethics will struggle and harm those around them.

outline.heading: The dropped stack of values
outline.gist: He imagines the Prophet stacking values in the right order and passing the stack down until someone dropped it and restacked it wrongly; the damage only shows generations later, and we are still trying to restore the order.

outline.heading: Outro

ytb2-rSF6KQ.title: The Values of Islam: Righteousness, Justice and Refusing Oppression
ytb2-rSF6KQ.one_line: Rights come only from Allah, justice is applying them, and refusing oppression outweighs every other value, shown through the stolen shield and Badr.
ytb2-rSF6KQ.summary: He argues that only Allah can grant true rights; anything humans grant is a privilege that can be withdrawn, which is why the world values Gaza's children less than others. From rights comes justice, and both rest on haqq, righteousness. Many unethical people believe they are ethical because their values are confused about whose rights exist. Justice has a counterpart: even when what is fair is unclear, oppression is usually recognizable, and Allah forbade it upon Himself out of His own generosity in granting us rights. Once a violated right is identified, it outweighs every other consideration. He illustrates with the Quran exonerating a Jewish man framed for a theft committed by Muslims, despite the turmoil it caused, and the Prophet saying he would apply the law even to his own daughter. Muslims must speak the truth even against themselves, and teach children rights before other virtues; tribal refusals to marry 'those people' deny Allah-given equality. At Badr the Companions were sent to reclaim wealth seized from them, because one must never meekly surrender one's rights. He closes with a village practice of pressuring sisters to waive inheritance and vows to stand against any oppressor whatever the faith of oppressor or oppressed.

outline.heading: Rights versus privileges
outline.gist: Humans can only grant privileges that can be revoked; this is why Gaza's children are treated as worth less than others.

outline.heading: The rights Allah grants every human
outline.gist: Life, learning, equality, property, expression and dignity are decreed by Allah and cannot be taken away.

outline.heading: Justice depends on knowing the rights
outline.gist: If people were not equal, justice would differ by who you are; without clear rights we cannot judge properly.

outline.heading: The unethical who think they are ethical
outline.gist: Confused values about rights produce people who cannot see their own wrong; the Quran details the rights of men, women, the weak and even animals.

outline.heading: Speaking the truth without fear of people
outline.gist: Rights survive only if people speak up; justice has a counterpart value, the refusal of oppression.

outline.heading: How could Allah oppress? Rights granted by His will
outline.gist: Allah forbade oppression upon Himself; He owes us nothing, yet chose to declare rights and bind Himself to them.

outline.heading: You can always see oppression
outline.gist: Even when justice is unclear, oppression is visible, so Islamic ethics absolutely refuses it.

outline.heading: Haqq outweighs every other value
outline.gist: Once you identify a violated right, niceness and other considerations fall away; the challenge is learning to identify it.

outline.heading: The stolen shield and the framed Jewish neighbour
outline.gist: Three young men stole food and a valuable shield, buried it in a Jewish man's yard and pointed suspicion at him.

outline.heading: Revelation exonerates the innocent outsider
outline.gist: Verses came at night forbidding defence of the traitors; the Quran cleared a man of another faith and blamed Muslims despite the turmoil.

outline.heading: Equality before the law: even the Prophet's daughter
outline.gist: The law applies to everyone or to no one; say the truth even against yourself.

outline.heading: Confessing against yourself and teaching children rights first
outline.gist: Unlike Western law, Islam calls you to admit your own wrong; teach children rights before kindness and loyalty.

outline.heading: Denying Allah-given equality
outline.gist: Families refuse to marry from 'those people' who share their names and ancestry, rejecting what Allah decreed.

outline.heading: Badr: why go after the caravan
outline.gist: A small, outnumbered community questioned provoking Quraysh, but Quraysh had seized the emigrants' homes and wealth.

outline.heading: What Islam is designed to protect
outline.gist: Life, belief, wealth, dignity and intellect; Quraysh violated both property and freedom of belief.

outline.heading: Never meekly surrender your rights
outline.gist: The verses of Anfal show it was about rights, not money; claim your right first, then gift it if you wish.

outline.heading: Sisters pressured to waive inheritance
outline.gist: In his village a sheikh insisted the sister first receive her share; once given, it never came back.

outline.heading: Standing against every oppressor
outline.gist: Nothing weighs more than haqq and justice; he opposes oppression whatever the religion of oppressor or oppressed.

outline.heading: Outro
