stories.who: The companions at Uhud (3:155)
stories.point: Great men turned their backs because Shaytan exploited weaknesses they already had; he waits for the right moment to use old sins.

stories.who: Iblis's challenge to Allah (17:62-65)
stories.point: Shaytan announced his plan openly: incite, assault, share in wealth and children, make false promises; Allah's true servants are beyond his authority.

stories.who: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, Malik, Sufyan, Qatadah, Al-Aswad and Al-A'mash in Ramadan
stories.point: The salaf set aside hadith, fiqh and grammar when Ramadan came and devoted themselves to the Quran, completing it every ten, five, two or one nights.

contemporary: Overflow crowds at the London masjid in the first nights of Ramadan 1447: closed rooms opened and people praying outside in the cold
Scrolling, clicking and messaging as the habits of the nafs that continue even with Shaytan chained
takeaways: Renew the intention you had before Ramadan to make this month the one that changes you
Identify the specific weaknesses Shaytan exploited during the year and write them down
Identify the weaknesses of your own nafs: whatever you still do while Shaytan is chained is your own habit, so work on it now
Make lifestyle changes: sleep early, change what you do at the hours when sins happen, come to the masjid, eat less before prayer
Devote the rest of the month to the Quran, sujood and dua as the salaf did, and do not drop off after the first week

6:158.ar: هَلۡ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَّآ أَن تَأۡتِيَهُمُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ أَوۡ يَأۡتِيَ رَبُّكَ أَوۡ يَأۡتِيَ بَعۡضُ ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّكَۗ يَوۡمَ يَأۡتِي بَعۡضُ ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّكَ لَا يَنفَعُ نَفۡسًا إِيمَٰنُهَا لَمۡ تَكُنۡ ءَامَنَتۡ مِن قَبۡلُ أَوۡ كَسَبَتۡ فِيٓ إِيمَٰنِهَا خَيۡرࣰ اۗ قُلِ ٱنتَظِرُوٓاْ إِنَّا مُنتَظِرُونَ
6:158.en: Do they [then] wait for anything except that the angels should come to them or your Lord should come or that there come some of the signs of your Lord? The Day that some of the signs of your Lord will come no soul will benefit from its faith as long as it had not believed before or had earned through its faith some good. Say, "Wait. Indeed, we [also] are waiting

52:21.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَٱتَّبَعَتۡهُمۡ ذُرِّيَّتُهُم بِإِيمَٰنٍ أَلۡحَقۡنَا بِهِمۡ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمۡ وَمَآ أَلَتۡنَٰهُم مِّنۡ عَمَلِهِم مِّن شَيۡءࣲۚ كُلُّ ٱمۡرِيِٕۭ بِمَا كَسَبَ رَهِينࣱ‏
52:21.en: And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith - We will join with them their descendants, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds. Every person, for what he earned, is retained

16:111.ar: ۞يَوۡمَ تَأۡتِي كُلُّ نَفۡسࣲ تُجَٰدِلُ عَن نَّفۡسِهَا وَتُوَفَّىٰ كُلُّ نَفۡسࣲ مَّا عَمِلَتۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ
16:111.en: On the Day when every soul will come disputing for itself, and every soul will be fully compensated for what it did, and they will not be wronged

66:6.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ قُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ وَأَهۡلِيكُمۡ نَارࣰ ا وَقُودُهَا ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱلۡحِجَارَةُ عَلَيۡهَا مَلَٰٓئِكَةٌ غِلَاظࣱ شِدَادࣱ لَّا يَعۡصُونَ ٱللَّهَ مَآ أَمَرَهُمۡ وَيَفۡعَلُونَ مَا يُؤۡمَرُونَ
66:6.en: O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are [appointed] angels, harsh and severe; they do not disobey Allah in what He commands them but do what they are commanded

26:214.en: And warn, [O Muhammad], your closest kindred

-hQ3VyHeqxQ.speaker: adnan
-hQ3VyHeqxQ.speaker_note: Speaks as the masjid's imam and refers to his own children and parents; no other speaker named
-hQ3VyHeqxQ.title: Ramadan Preparation: Focusing on One's Self
-hQ3VyHeqxQ.one_line: Before Ramadan 1447: be a little selfish, sit honestly with yourself, run from the fire and live clean for thirty days.
-hQ3VyHeqxQ.summary: A khutbah given six days before Ramadan 1447, built on one instruction: this year, focus on yourself. He opens with 6:158 (faith will not help the soul that waits for the decisive signs) and 16:111 (every soul will come arguing for itself alone), and says the community's battery is empty after a hard year. Ramadan is the chance to sit in a session of self-honesty and ask where you are and whether you have drifted. Citing 66:6, he says Allah placed the fire where you can see it so you would run from it, and placed His love in the escape route: make escaping punishment your only goal and Jannah and love follow as consequences. As a father he would stand in for his children on that Day but cannot, and intercession comes later, so be a little selfish. His practical advice is to live clean for thirty days: strip social media and music from the phone, read Quran or reflect when you reach for it, fix your sleep. Hunger while fasting is a reminder that the spirit is hungrier still and needs its Lord. The second khutbah recounts the Prophet's first public sermon, in which he told even Fatima he could not save her from the fire, and the hadith qudsi on Allah loving the servant who keeps drawing near.

outline.heading: Opening
What are they waiting for? (6:158)
outline.gist: Are they waiting for the decisive signs of their Lord? When those signs come, faith will not benefit a soul that had not established it earlier or earned good through it. Do not wait.

outline.heading: Focus on yourself: every soul argues for itself
outline.gist: The battery is empty and we are running on fumes, so this Ramadan take for yourself what you need. Every person is held hostage by what they did; on that Day each soul comes to argue for itself alone and receives only the results of its own deeds.

outline.heading: A session of self-honesty
outline.gist: Sit with yourself honestly and ask: what do I seek, what do I need, where am I, where should I be going, am I still on track or have I drifted for a long time? Then 66:6: protect yourselves and your families from a fire fuelled by people and stones.

outline.heading: The fire in view, His love in the escape route
outline.gist: Allah placed the fire where you can see it so you would fear it and run the other way, and placed His love along your escape route. Ask to be freed from the chains that pull towards the fire, and you will find His love waiting.

outline.heading: Only one goal this year: escape punishment
outline.gist: Focus on not being punished; Jannah and loving Allah are natural consequences. On that Day you have nothing to argue with but your own choices, so focus on yourself, the only one you are responsible for.

outline.heading: No one can stand in for you: be a little selfish
outline.gist: As a father he wants to stand up and answer for his children, and for his parents, but cannot; intercession comes later, after each is held to account alone. So be a little selfish this year and make changes: live clean.

outline.heading: Live clean for thirty days
outline.gist: Strip social media from your phone, stop scrolling, and when you feel the urge to touch it, read Quran or reflect on a meaning you have not thought about in a while. Replace music with knowledge or a reciter you enjoy, and replace late nights with a better sleep schedule.

outline.heading: The hunger of the spirit
outline.gist: Try it for thirty days and you will feel different. A few hours without food or coffee and our temper frays with the children; the spirit's nourishment is its Lord, and it has been deprived far longer. Allah makes the body hungry to remind you the spirit is hungrier: give it one month out of twelve.

outline.heading: Ramadan is a miracle worker
outline.gist: Whatever you have done, Ramadan can put you back on track, changing you from the inside out. Less phone and scrolling, more sitting with your hands raised speaking to Allah.

outline.heading: A dua for yourself and the ummah
outline.gist: He models it: what you need, fear, lost and hope for, then the ummah, the children, the poor and the weak with no one to speak for them, starving and oppressed while you have more than you need. More of that this year, and you will find what you are looking for.

outline.heading: Make the full intention now
outline.gist: He does not know whether he will reach this Ramadan, let alone the next, so make a powerful intention now to use the month fully; if your days run out, you enter the grave with that intention and its reward.

outline.heading: Interlude
The Prophet's first public sermon
outline.gist: Commanded to warn his family at the start of his prophethood (26:214), he gathered them in the first sermon we have on record, and began by praising, magnifying and exalting Allah.

outline.heading: Save yourselves; I cannot do it for you
outline.gist: One responsible for others does not lie to them, and he warned of a severe punishment. To each tribe he said: save yourselves from the fire, for I cannot. He would have done it for them, but he could only teach them how to save themselves; they had to choose.

outline.heading: Fatima: all my wealth, but not the fire
outline.gist: O Fatima, daughter of Muhammad, ask me for whatever you want of my wealth, but I cannot save you from the fire. Make that the plan this Ramadan: sit with ourselves and save ourselves.

outline.heading: Draw near until He loves you
outline.gist: Pray every night to save yourself and you reach the hadith qudsi: My servant keeps drawing near to Me with extra worship until I love him; then he sees, hears and walks through Me, and if he asks I give him and if he seeks refuge I grant it.

outline.heading: Outro

0MS2XrXEbbQ.speaker: adnan
0MS2XrXEbbQ.speaker_note: Series host; recaps the mortality module then takes comments and questions from attendees
0MS2XrXEbbQ.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Mortality, Episode 32 (Recap and Q&A)
0MS2XrXEbbQ.one_line: Recap of the mortality module and open Q&A: death as balance, anger for truth versus ego, teaching youth, remembering death, and planning.
0MS2XrXEbbQ.summary: He recaps the module: accepting death passes through grief toward acceptance, and once accepted it balances life, softening sadness, tempering success before it turns to arrogance, and freeing a person to hold to principle without fear. Accountability is what gives morality meaning and is the strongest leverage over the ego. The honest stance is that a long life is hoped for but never guaranteed, so prepare as one does with safety rules. An attendee then describes his own cancer and his daughter's lymphoma, and how unprepared he felt despite years of reflection. In answering questions, the sheikh distinguishes anger for the truth from anger for the self, pointing to the Prophet who never grew angry on his own behalf, and advises holding back any emotion whose motive is unclear while still standing by what is right. He explains that awareness of death should give young people urgency and love for time, not gloom, and that it must be presented in terms they understand, which requires a culture of mentorship where excellence becomes the norm. Death is best remembered through real experiences like attending burials and reading how righteous people died, and by making it a priority. He ends by saying one should plan worldly projects as if living forever and prepare for Allah as if tonight is the last night, and urges full commitment in Ramadan.

outline.heading: Opening
Recap: accepting death like working through grief
outline.gist: Understanding death brings initial sadness, then acceptance, and becomes a strong motive to make things end well.

outline.heading: Remembering death balances sadness, injustice and success
outline.gist: It eases loss, makes one pity the oppressor, and stops success from turning into vanity; nobody remembers the giants of 1934.

outline.heading: Death does not ruin good moments, it gives them perspective
outline.gist: If remembering death spoils your joy, you are too happy; it should turn success into gratitude.

outline.heading: Accepting death frees you to keep your principles
outline.gist: If fear of death trumps honesty or commitment, you are only good until threatened.

outline.heading: Without accountability morality is meaningless
outline.gist: Even the worst people are forgotten; only accountability gives morality a reason.

outline.heading: Death as the weapon that controls the nafs
outline.gist: The ego fears nothing like death; until you master your own fear of it, struggle against the self fails.

outline.heading: The truthful statement about your lifespan
outline.gist: You will probably live long, but sudden death is never impossible; prepare as safety laws prepare for unlikely accidents.

outline.heading: Interlude
An attendee's cancer diagnosis
outline.gist: An attendee recounts being diagnosed with stomach cancer and collapsing in the clinic despite years of reflecting on death.

outline.heading: His daughter's lymphoma and total reliance on Allah
outline.gist: Days after his surgery his daughter was diagnosed with a rare lymphoma; he found himself relying on Allah alone.

outline.heading: What the ordeal revealed: lack of preparation
outline.gist: He attributes the shock to unpreparedness and praises defining oneself through roles and values, which needs a mentor.

outline.heading: Islam gives a comforting account of death
outline.gist: Death strikes people very differently; Muslims need not patch together a philosophy because Allah has explained it.

outline.heading: Interlude
Question: anger for the truth or for the ego?
outline.gist: How to stand for what is right while checking that the motive is Allah and not the self.

outline.heading: Most emotions can be self-serving
outline.gist: Love can be 'fish love' and empathy can be mere sympathy; tazkiyah is analysing why you feel what you feel.

outline.heading: The Prophet never grew angry for himself
outline.gist: He bore rude Bedouins with constant patience yet could not be stopped when a right of Allah or of others was violated.

outline.heading: Stand by the truth, hold back unclear emotion
outline.gist: He keeps rants he is unsure of to himself; say only what you are sure is for Allah and swallow the rest.

outline.heading: Real emotion versus self-value swings
outline.gist: Emotions driven by feeling more or less valued are fake; once self-value is stable, feelings become quieter but real.

outline.heading: Interlude
Awareness of death gives the young urgency, not gloom
outline.gist: Knowing time is finite should get a teenager off seven-hour gaming sessions and toward learning and loving people more.

outline.heading: Present it in terms the young can grasp
outline.gist: Youth hear 'prepare for death' as a call to be depressed; it must be framed through their experience.

outline.heading: Parents experience a thousand deaths
outline.gist: His once-invincible father aged, and his own son's childhood passed while he was busy; cherish people while you have them.

outline.heading: The gap between generations in how messages land
outline.gist: The same idea must be packaged differently for children, which is part of an imam's job and part of a parent's.

outline.heading: Children accept advice better from others
outline.gist: An attendee notes his children hear reminders about death from parents as criticism but accept them from teachers.

outline.heading: Building a mentorship culture
outline.gist: The Prophet paired newcomers with seniors in Madinah; mentorship cannot be forced but grows when people of all ages and skills are present.

outline.heading: Accepting a changing role
outline.gist: He once reached children with a motorcycle and soccer skills and can no longer; embrace a new role and let others take the old one.

outline.heading: Make excellence the norm for the next generation
outline.gist: When most young people learn their deen and excel, the expectation shifts and culture changes for generations.

outline.heading: Question: how to remember death regularly
outline.gist: An attendee asks what techniques keep death present beyond emotional highs.

outline.heading: Real experiences give the mind an image of death
outline.gist: Attending deaths and burials, like his uncle's, gives abstract death a concrete memory to return to.

outline.heading: Near-death moments and the companions' longing
outline.gist: His own brush with death humbles him instantly; the companions wept recalling the Prophet's death and waited to join him.

outline.heading: You remember what you prioritise
outline.gist: Repeated forgetting is neglect; mortality is one of the five pillars of tazkiyah and must sit high on the priority list.

outline.heading: Using the deaths of people you loved
outline.gist: The passing of a close friend becomes a reminder whenever he drifts; a recorded contemplation also works but takes more effort.

outline.heading: Damascus tradition of reading how the righteous died
outline.gist: A weekly reading of biographies that always records how each person's life ended brings one closer to readiness.

outline.heading: Question: is it arrogant to plan when life may end?
outline.gist: An attendee asks how to balance long-term planning with the reality that death may come first.

outline.heading: Plan the world as if forever, prepare as if tonight
outline.gist: Build sustainable, succession-minded plans for family and community while preparing your deeds as if you die tonight.

outline.heading: Remembering death makes long-term plans moral
outline.gist: You may not live to undo harm a plan causes, so mortality keeps planning free of corruption and mindful of legacy.

outline.heading: When he first reflected on death
outline.gist: Around grade seven in Makkah he told his mother to be ready for his death, and she cried all night.

outline.heading: Making dua for parents in prayer
outline.gist: Sujud is the best time; Arabic is preferred in obligatory prayer but other languages are permissible.

outline.heading: Aim high and you will not miss out on joy
outline.gist: Chasing fun loses it; dedicating yourself to a higher cause brings enjoyment of life with it.

outline.heading: The Prophet lived the fullest life despite every disadvantage
outline.gist: Orphaned, unschooled and raised by a busy uncle, he still lived without limits.

outline.heading: He rejected celibacy and self-denial
outline.gist: He corrected companions who vowed celibacy or constant fasting; monastic abstinence fails because it fights human nature.

outline.heading: Give yourself fully to Ramadan
outline.gist: Those working on their hearts should use Ramadan to repair defects and tame the ego that creeps back out by Sha'ban.

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And [mention, O Muhammad], when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority." They said, "Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we declare Your praise and sanctify You?" Allah said, "Indeed, I know that which you do not know

2:31.ar: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِي بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
2:31.en: And He taught Adam the names - all of them. Then He showed them to the angels and said, "Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful

2:32.ar: قَالُواْ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ لَا عِلۡمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمۡتَنَآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
2:32.en: They said, "Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, it is You who is the Knowing, the Wise

2:33.ar: قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ أَنۢبِئۡهُم بِأَسۡمَآئِهِمۡۖ فَلَمَّآ أَنۢبَأَهُم بِأَسۡمَآئِهِمۡ قَالَ أَلَمۡ أَقُل لَّكُمۡ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ غَيۡبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَأَعۡلَمُ مَا تُبۡدُونَ وَمَا كُنتُمۡ تَكۡتُمُونَ
2:33.en: He said, "O Adam, inform them of their names." And when he had informed them of their names, He said, "Did I not tell you that I know the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth? And I know what you reveal and what you have concealed

2:34.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُواْ لِأٓدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:34.en: And [mention] when We said to the angels, "Prostrate before Adam"; so they prostrated, except for Iblees. He refused and was arrogant and became of the disbelievers

2:35.ar: وَقُلۡنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسۡكُنۡ أَنتَ وَزَوۡجُكَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَكُلَا مِنۡهَا رَغَدًا حَيۡثُ شِئۡتُمَا وَلَا تَقۡرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:35.en: And We said, "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat therefrom in [ease and] abundance from wherever you will. But do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers

2:36.ar: فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ عَنۡهَا فَأَخۡرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِۖ وَقُلۡنَا ٱهۡبِطُواْ بَعۡضُكُمۡ لِبَعۡضٍ عَدُوࣱّۖ وَلَكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مُسۡتَقَرࣱّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينࣲ‏
2:36.en: But Satan caused them to slip out of it and removed them from that [condition] in which they had been. And We said, "Go down, [all of you], as enemies to one another, and you will have upon the earth a place of settlement and provision for a time

2:37.ar: فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَٰتࣲ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡهِۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:37.en: Then Adam received from his Lord [some] words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful

2:38.ar: قُلۡنَا ٱهۡبِطُواْ مِنۡهَا جَمِيعࣰ اۖ فَإِمَّا يَأۡتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّي هُدࣰ ى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَايَ فَلَا خَوۡفٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحۡزَنُونَ
2:38.en: We said, "Go down from it, all of you. And when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve

2:39.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَكَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
2:39.en: And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs - those will be companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally

2:92.ar: ۞وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَكُم مُّوسَىٰ بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ ثُمَّ ٱتَّخَذۡتُمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ وَأَنتُمۡ ظَٰلِمُونَ
2:92.en: And Moses had certainly brought you clear proofs. Then you took the calf [in worship] after that, while you were wrongdoers

2:93.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذۡنَا مِيثَٰقَكُمۡ وَرَفَعۡنَا فَوۡقَكُمُ ٱلطُّورَ خُذُواْ مَآ ءَاتَيۡنَٰكُم بِقُوَّةࣲ وَٱسۡمَعُواْۖ قَالُواْ سَمِعۡنَا وَعَصَيۡنَا وَأُشۡرِبُواْ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ بِكُفۡرِهِمۡۚ قُلۡ بِئۡسَمَا يَأۡمُرُكُم بِهِۦٓ إِيمَٰنُكُمۡ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
2:93.en: And [recall] when We took your covenant and raised over you the mount, [saying], "Take what We have given you with determination and listen." They said [instead], "We hear and disobey." And their hearts absorbed [the worship of] the calf because of their disbelief. Say, "How wretched is that which your faith enjoins upon you, if you should be believers

2:94.ar: قُلۡ إِن كَانَتۡ لَكُمُ ٱلدَّارُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ خَالِصَةࣰ مِّن دُونِ ٱلنَّاسِ فَتَمَنَّوُاْ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
2:94.en: Say, [O Muhammad], "If the home of the Hereafter with Allah is for you alone and not the [other] people, then wish for death, if you should be truthful

2:95.ar: وَلَن يَتَمَنَّوۡهُ أَبَدَۢا بِمَا قَدَّمَتۡ أَيۡدِيهِمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمُۢ بِٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:95.en: But they will never wish for it, ever, because of what their hands have put forth. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers

2:96.ar: وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمۡ أَحۡرَصَ ٱلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ حَيَوٰةࣲ وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَشۡرَكُواْۚ يَوَدُّ أَحَدُهُمۡ لَوۡ يُعَمَّرُ أَلۡفَ سَنَةࣲ وَمَا هُوَ بِمُزَحۡزِحِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ أَن يُعَمَّرَۗ وَٱللَّهُ بَصِيرُۢ بِمَا يَعۡمَلُونَ
2:96.en: And you will surely find them the most greedy of people for life - [even] more than those who associate others with Allah. One of them wishes that he could be granted life a thousand years, but it would not remove him in the least from the [coming] punishment that he should be granted life. And Allah is Seeing of what they do

2:124.ar: ۞وَإِذِ ٱبۡتَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ رَبُّهُۥ بِكَلِمَٰتࣲ فَأَتَمَّهُنَّۖ قَالَ إِنِّي جَاعِلُكَ لِلنَّاسِ إِمَامࣰ اۖ قَالَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِيۖ قَالَ لَا يَنَالُ عَهۡدِي ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:124.en: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham was tried by his Lord with commands and he fulfilled them. [Allah] said, "Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people." [Abraham] said, "And of my descendants?" [Allah] said, "My covenant does not include the wrongdoers

20:120.ar: فَوَسۡوَسَ إِلَيۡهِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلۡخُلۡدِ وَمُلۡكࣲ لَّا يَبۡلَىٰ
20:120.en: Then Satan whispered to him; he said, "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and possession that will not deteriorate

7:23.ar: قَالَا رَبَّنَا ظَلَمۡنَآ أَنفُسَنَا وَإِن لَّمۡ تَغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَتَرۡحَمۡنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
7:23.en: They said, "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers

Qkj0rW5zlLs.speaker: adnan
Qkj0rW5zlLs.speaker_note: Sheikh Adnan's Ramadan Quranic Themes series; refers to his 13 years serving the community here
Qkj0rW5zlLs.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 1: Quranic Themes 2 - Stewardship
Qkj0rW5zlLs.one_line: Opening the second Quranic Themes series with stewardship (khilafah), read through Adam, the Children of Israel and Ibrahim in Al-Baqarah.
Qkj0rW5zlLs.summary: He opens the year's series by explaining that the Quran returns to themes rather than repeating itself, because a concept only lands when it is approached several times in different ways. The first theme is stewardship: the human being is a khalifa, not in a political sense but as someone left responsible for things on another's behalf, who will be asked how he cared for them. He reads three passages of Al-Baqarah as three kinds of steward. Adam failed his first test because he did not yet understand his own nafs and disliked being responsible, mortal and a servant; he repented with the words Allah gave him and never knowingly disobeyed again, and we are handed his lesson without paying his price. The Children of Israel are the example of failure: after clear signs they took the calf, said they hear and disobey, and their hearts were soaked in that love until it could not be removed; and they became greedy for mere life, a fear of death that makes a person sell out every principle. Ibrahim is the steward who passed test after test and was made an imam. He asks listeners to take responsibility seriously, use Ramadan to wash out sins that have settled in the heart, and rank values above survival.

outline.heading: The Quran teaches through themes, not repetition
outline.gist: The Quran revisits major and minor themes so a concept can be absorbed slowly; last year covered 29 themes and this year adds another set.

outline.heading: Stewardship as the human job description
outline.gist: A steward is responsible for something on someone else's behalf; the human being is a khalifa spiritually, not politically, and worships Allah through that responsibility and will be asked about it.

outline.heading: Interlude
Adam placed on earth as a khalifa
outline.gist: Adam begins like any of us, enjoying breath, food and companionship without yet knowing why, and is told he will be a steward on earth.

outline.heading: The tree: failing a test before knowing the self
outline.gist: Adam ate not out of evil or ingratitude but because he had not yet understood his nafs; Shaytan exploited this with the lie of immortality.

outline.heading: Three truths the nafs dislikes
outline.gist: Adam was uncomfortable being responsible, being mortal and being a servant, the same three things people resist today.

outline.heading: Sent down: shame and loss
outline.gist: On earth Adam lost safety, plenty and companionship, but what hurt most was the shame of having disobeyed Allah.

outline.heading: Words of repentance given to Adam
outline.gist: Not yet knowing what tawbah was, Adam was taught words to say, admitting he had wronged himself, and Allah accepted his repentance.

outline.heading: A scripted lesson, not a return to Paradise
outline.gist: Adam was still sent down because earth was his purpose; the episode teaches obedience, restraining the nafs and owning responsibility for oneself and one's family.

outline.heading: Follow the guidance; Adam never knowingly sinned again
outline.gist: Whoever follows Allah's guidance has nothing to fear; we receive the solved example for free, and Adam's later mistakes were only forgetfulness and lack of knowledge.

outline.heading: Interlude
Taking the calf after clear signs
outline.gist: Stewardship is both obligation and opportunity; Allah teaches it through good and failed examples, starting with a people who worshipped the calf after Musa's miracles.

outline.heading: The covenant under the raised mountain
outline.gist: Their covenant was renewed under the mountain; the Torah taught the same responsibility the Quran teaches, to shepherd the wellbeing of those around you.

outline.heading: Hearts soaked in the love of the calf
outline.gist: The word for 'made to drink' means soaked through; sin becomes deadly when it stays in the heart until it cannot be separated, like cloth left in perfume or sewage.

outline.heading: Ramadan can rid the heart of a soaked sin
outline.gist: A sin that persists despite knowing it is haram has been absorbed by the heart; Ramadan is a rare chance to remove it, and stewardship is impossible without doing so.

outline.heading: Greed for mere life
outline.gist: Being the most eager for life means a crippling fear of death; such a person will compromise any principle and cannot even trust himself to protect his own family.

outline.heading: A steward's priorities are values, in the right order
outline.gist: Muslims need to know not only Islam's values and ethics but how they rank, otherwise they discard a value that should never be dropped.

outline.heading: Our heroes stood their ground under threat
outline.gist: Prolonging life is not a value in itself; the people we honour held to their principles with a gun to their heads, which is what stewardship and manhood mean.

outline.heading: Three kinds of steward
outline.gist: Adam erred then got it right, the Children of Israel kept failing by choice, and Ibrahim got it right without the initial mistake.

outline.heading: Ibrahim tested with trial after trial
outline.gist: Ibrahim spoke against his people's idols, was thrown into the fire, expelled, debated star worshippers and a king, and passed every test.

outline.heading: Made an imam for mankind
outline.gist: Allah made him a leader; he died with few followers yet is now honoured by most of humanity, and he then asked about his descendants.

themes.label: Stewardship (khilafah) and human responsibility
themes.note: The human being is a khalifa responsible for self, family and community, and the three Baqarah passages show stewardship lived badly, recovered and done well.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Stewardship is presented as the answer to what we are here for beyond eating, drinking and greeting each other.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Adam's creation, test, fall and repentance read as a model lesson every person repeats.

themes.label: Tazkiyah: purifying and training the self
themes.note: Adam failed because he did not yet understand his nafs and its resistance to responsibility, mortality and servitude.

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: Allah taught Adam the words of repentance, and after it Adam never knowingly crossed the line again.

themes.label: Sins, their causes and remedies
themes.note: A sin left in the heart soaks into it until it cannot be removed, which is how addiction to sin forms.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: Ramadan is one of the few opportunities to wash out a sin the heart has absorbed.

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it
themes.note: Greed for life is a fear of death that makes a person compromise every principle and untrustworthy as a steward.

themes.label: Values, principles and ethics as a system
themes.note: Muslims must know Islam's values and their ranking so they do not replace a higher value with a lower one.

themes.label: Courage and commitment
themes.note: The people we honour held their ground even at the cost of their lives.

quran.point: Shaytan's lie that the tree would bring immortality
The words of repentance Adam and his wife were taught: we have wronged ourselves

maxims: The Quran is not repetition; it is a thematic approach
Saying it once never works
You're a khalifa: not politically, but spiritually and humanely
The problem with sin is that it stays in your heart
If just living is your priority, you cannot be trusted

stories.who: Adam and the tree
stories.point: Failure came from not understanding the nafs; repentance and never knowingly repeating the sin is the path back.

stories.who: The Children of Israel and the golden calf
stories.point: A sin left to soak in the heart and an obsession with survival strip a people of their ability to be stewards.

stories.who: Ibrahim's trials
stories.point: Passing test after test earns leadership and a legacy far larger than one's following in life.

takeaways: See yourself as a steward who will be asked how you cared for yourself, your family and your community.
Use Ramadan to uproot a sin that has settled in your heart before it becomes permanent.
When you slip, repent as Adam did and never knowingly return to the same sin.
Do not let fear of death or love of comfort push you to compromise your principles.
Learn the values of Islam and their order of priority so you argue from the right ethic.

1:1.en: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful

1:2.en: [All] praise is [due] to Allah, Lord of the worlds

1:3.en: The Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful

1:4.en: Sovereign of the Day of Recompense

1:5.en: It is You we worship and You we ask for help

1:6.en: Guide us to the straight path

1:7.ar: صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ غَيۡرِ ٱلۡمَغۡضُوبِ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
1:7.en: The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have evoked [Your] anger or of those who are astray

2:2.ar: ذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ لَا رَيۡبَۛ فِيهِۛ هُدࣰ ى لِّلۡمُتَّقِينَ
2:2.en: This is the Book about which there is no doubt, a guidance for those conscious of Allah

2:3.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَيُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
2:3.en: Who believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and spend out of what We have provided for them

2:4.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبۡلِكَ وَبِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ هُمۡ يُوقِنُونَ
2:4.en: And who believe in what has been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what was revealed before you, and of the Hereafter they are certain [in faith]

2:5.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ عَلَىٰ هُدࣰ ى مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
2:5.en: Those are upon [right] guidance from their Lord, and it is those who are the successful

2:6.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَأَنذَرۡتَهُمۡ أَمۡ لَمۡ تُنذِرۡهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
2:6.en: Indeed, those who disbelieve - it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe

2:7.ar: خَتَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمۡ وَعَلَىٰ سَمۡعِهِمۡۖ وَعَلَىٰٓ أَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡ غِشَٰوَةࣱۖ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
2:7.en: Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their vision is a veil. And for them is a great punishment

2:8.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَبِٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَمَا هُم بِمُؤۡمِنِينَ
2:8.en: And of the people are some who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers

2:9.ar: يُخَٰدِعُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَمَا يَخۡدَعُونَ إِلَّآ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَمَا يَشۡعُرُونَ
2:9.en: They [think to] deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive not except themselves and perceive [it] not

2:10.ar: فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضࣱ فَزَادَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مَرَضࣰ اۖ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمُۢ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكۡذِبُونَ
2:10.en: In their hearts is disease, so Allah has increased their disease; and for them is a painful punishment because they [habitually] used to lie

2:11.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمۡ لَا تُفۡسِدُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّمَا نَحۡنُ مُصۡلِحُونَ
2:11.en: And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are but reformers

2:12.ar: أَلَآ إِنَّهُمۡ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدُونَ وَلَٰكِن لَّا يَشۡعُرُونَ
2:12.en: Unquestionably, it is they who are the corrupters, but they perceive [it] not

2:13.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمۡ ءَامِنُواْ كَمَآ ءَامَنَ ٱلنَّاسُ قَالُوٓاْ أَنُؤۡمِنُ كَمَآ ءَامَنَ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُۗ أَلَآ إِنَّهُمۡ هُمُ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ وَلَٰكِن لَّا يَعۡلَمُونَ
2:13.en: And when it is said to them, "Believe as the people have believed," they say, "Should we believe as the foolish have believed?" Unquestionably, it is they who are the foolish, but they know [it] not

2:14.ar: وَإِذَا لَقُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ قَالُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ شَيَٰطِينِهِمۡ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا مَعَكُمۡ إِنَّمَا نَحۡنُ مُسۡتَهۡزِءُونَ
2:14.en: And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with their evil ones, they say, "Indeed, we are with you; we were only mockers

2:15.ar: ٱللَّهُ يَسۡتَهۡزِئُ بِهِمۡ وَيَمُدُّهُمۡ فِي طُغۡيَٰنِهِمۡ يَعۡمَهُونَ
2:15.en: [But] Allah mocks them and prolongs them in their transgression [while] they wander blindly

2:16.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱشۡتَرَوُاْ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةَ بِٱلۡهُدَىٰ فَمَا رَبِحَت تِّجَٰرَتُهُمۡ وَمَا كَانُواْ مُهۡتَدِينَ
2:16.en: Those are the ones who have purchased error [in exchange] for guidance, so their transaction has brought no profit, nor were they guided

2:17.ar: مَثَلُهُمۡ كَمَثَلِ ٱلَّذِي ٱسۡتَوۡقَدَ نَارࣰ ا فَلَمَّآ أَضَآءَتۡ مَا حَوۡلَهُۥ ذَهَبَ ٱللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمۡ وَتَرَكَهُمۡ فِي ظُلُمَٰتࣲ لَّا يُبۡصِرُونَ
2:17.en: Their example is that of one who kindled a fire, but when it illuminated what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darkness [so] they could not see

2:18.ar: صُمُّۢ بُكۡمٌ عُمۡيࣱ فَهُمۡ لَا يَرۡجِعُونَ
2:18.en: Deaf, dumb and blind - so they will not return [to the right path]

2:19.ar: أَوۡ كَصَيِّبࣲ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فِيهِ ظُلُمَٰتࣱ وَرَعۡدࣱ وَبَرۡقࣱ يَجۡعَلُونَ أَصَٰبِعَهُمۡ فِيٓ ءَاذَانِهِم مِّنَ ٱلصَّوَٰعِقِ حَذَرَ ٱلۡمَوۡتِۚ وَٱللَّهُ مُحِيطُۢ بِٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:19.en: Or [it is] like a rainstorm from the sky within which is darkness, thunder and lightning. They put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps in dread of death. But Allah is encompassing of the disbelievers

2:20.ar: يَكَادُ ٱلۡبَرۡقُ يَخۡطَفُ أَبۡصَٰرَهُمۡۖ كُلَّمَآ أَضَآءَ لَهُم مَّشَوۡاْ فِيهِ وَإِذَآ أَظۡلَمَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ قَامُواْۚ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَذَهَبَ بِسَمۡعِهِمۡ وَأَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
2:20.en: The lightning almost snatches away their sight. Every time it lights [the way] for them, they walk therein; but when darkness comes over them, they stand [still]. And if Allah had willed, He could have taken away their hearing and their sight. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent

2:21.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱعۡبُدُواْ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُمۡ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
2:21.en: O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, that you may become righteous

2:22.ar: ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فِرَٰشࣰ ا وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بِنَآءࣰ وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَخۡرَجَ بِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ رِزۡقࣰ ا لَّكُمۡۖ فَلَا تَجۡعَلُواْ لِلَّهِ أَندَادࣰ ا وَأَنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:22.en: [He] who made for you the earth a bed [spread out] and the sky a ceiling and sent down from the sky, rain and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you. So do not attribute to Allah equals while you know [that there is nothing similar to Him]

2:23.ar: وَإِن كُنتُمۡ فِي رَيۡبࣲ مِّمَّا نَزَّلۡنَا عَلَىٰ عَبۡدِنَا فَأۡتُواْ بِسُورَةࣲ مِّن مِّثۡلِهِۦ وَٱدۡعُواْ شُهَدَآءَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
2:23.en: And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our Servant [Muhammad], then produce a surah the like thereof and call upon your witnesses other than Allah, if you should be truthful

2:24.ar: فَإِن لَّمۡ تَفۡعَلُواْ وَلَن تَفۡعَلُواْ فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱلنَّارَ ٱلَّتِي وَقُودُهَا ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱلۡحِجَارَةُۖ أُعِدَّتۡ لِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:24.en: But if you do not - and you will never be able to - then fear the Fire, whose fuel is men and stones, prepared for the disbelievers

2:25.ar: وَبَشِّرِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ أَنَّ لَهُمۡ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُۖ كُلَّمَا رُزِقُواْ مِنۡهَا مِن ثَمَرَةࣲ رِّزۡقࣰ ا قَالُواْ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي رُزِقۡنَا مِن قَبۡلُۖ وَأُتُواْ بِهِۦ مُتَشَٰبِهࣰ اۖ وَلَهُمۡ فِيهَآ أَزۡوَٰجࣱ مُّطَهَّرَةࣱۖ وَهُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
2:25.en: And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds that they will have gardens [in Paradise] beneath which rivers flow. Whenever they are provided with a provision of fruit therefrom, they will say, "This is what we were provided with before." And it is given to them in likeness. And they will have therein purified spouses, and they will abide therein eternally

2:26.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَسۡتَحۡيِۦٓ أَن يَضۡرِبَ مَثَلࣰ ا مَّا بَعُوضَةࣰ فَمَا فَوۡقَهَاۚ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ فَيَعۡلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡۖ وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَيَقُولُونَ مَاذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَٰذَا مَثَلࣰ اۘ يُضِلُّ بِهِۦ كَثِيرࣰ ا وَيَهۡدِي بِهِۦ كَثِيرࣰ اۚ وَمَا يُضِلُّ بِهِۦٓ إِلَّا ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
2:26.en: Indeed, Allah is not timid to present an example - that of a mosquito or what is smaller than it. And those who have believed know that it is the truth from their Lord. But as for those who disbelieve, they say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?" He misleads many thereby and guides many thereby. And He misleads not except the defiantly disobedient

2:27.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَنقُضُونَ عَهۡدَ ٱللَّهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مِيثَٰقِهِۦ وَيَقۡطَعُونَ مَآ أَمَرَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦٓ أَن يُوصَلَ وَيُفۡسِدُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡخَٰسِرُونَ
2:27.en: Who break the covenant of Allah after contracting it and sever that which Allah has ordered to be joined and cause corruption on earth. It is those who are the losers

2:28.ar: كَيۡفَ تَكۡفُرُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَكُنتُمۡ أَمۡوَٰتࣰ ا فَأَحۡيَٰكُمۡۖ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمۡ ثُمَّ يُحۡيِيكُمۡ ثُمَّ إِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
2:28.en: How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were lifeless and He brought you to life; then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you [back] to life, and then to Him you will be returned

2:29.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَسَوَّىٰهُنَّ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَٰتࣲۚ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣱ‏
2:29.en: It is He who created for you all of that which is on the earth. Then He directed Himself to the heaven, [His being above all creation], and made them seven heavens, and He is Knowing of all things

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And [mention, O Muhammad], when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority." They said, "Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we declare Your praise and sanctify You?" Allah said, "Indeed, I know that which you do not know

2:31.ar: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِي بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
2:31.en: And He taught Adam the names - all of them. Then He showed them to the angels and said, "Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful

2:32.ar: قَالُواْ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ لَا عِلۡمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمۡتَنَآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
2:32.en: They said, "Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, it is You who is the Knowing, the Wise

2:33.ar: قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ أَنۢبِئۡهُم بِأَسۡمَآئِهِمۡۖ فَلَمَّآ أَنۢبَأَهُم بِأَسۡمَآئِهِمۡ قَالَ أَلَمۡ أَقُل لَّكُمۡ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ غَيۡبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَأَعۡلَمُ مَا تُبۡدُونَ وَمَا كُنتُمۡ تَكۡتُمُونَ
2:33.en: He said, "O Adam, inform them of their names." And when he had informed them of their names, He said, "Did I not tell you that I know the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth? And I know what you reveal and what you have concealed

2:34.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُواْ لِأٓدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:34.en: And [mention] when We said to the angels, "Prostrate before Adam"; so they prostrated, except for Iblees. He refused and was arrogant and became of the disbelievers

2:35.ar: وَقُلۡنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسۡكُنۡ أَنتَ وَزَوۡجُكَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَكُلَا مِنۡهَا رَغَدًا حَيۡثُ شِئۡتُمَا وَلَا تَقۡرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:35.en: And We said, "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat therefrom in [ease and] abundance from wherever you will. But do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers

2:36.ar: فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ عَنۡهَا فَأَخۡرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِۖ وَقُلۡنَا ٱهۡبِطُواْ بَعۡضُكُمۡ لِبَعۡضٍ عَدُوࣱّۖ وَلَكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مُسۡتَقَرࣱّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينࣲ‏
2:36.en: But Satan caused them to slip out of it and removed them from that [condition] in which they had been. And We said, "Go down, [all of you], as enemies to one another, and you will have upon the earth a place of settlement and provision for a time

2:37.ar: فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَٰتࣲ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡهِۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:37.en: Then Adam received from his Lord [some] words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful

2:38.ar: قُلۡنَا ٱهۡبِطُواْ مِنۡهَا جَمِيعࣰ اۖ فَإِمَّا يَأۡتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّي هُدࣰ ى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَايَ فَلَا خَوۡفٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحۡزَنُونَ
2:38.en: We said, "Go down from it, all of you. And when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve

2:39.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَكَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
2:39.en: And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs - those will be companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally

2:40.ar: يَٰبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَتِيَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنۡعَمۡتُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَأَوۡفُواْ بِعَهۡدِيٓ أُوفِ بِعَهۡدِكُمۡ وَإِيَّٰيَ فَٱرۡهَبُونِ
2:40.en: O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you and fulfill My covenant [upon you] that I will fulfill your covenant [from Me], and be afraid of [only] Me

2:41.ar: وَءَامِنُواْ بِمَآ أَنزَلۡتُ مُصَدِّقࣰ ا لِّمَا مَعَكُمۡ وَلَا تَكُونُوٓاْ أَوَّلَ كَافِرِۭ بِهِۦۖ وَلَا تَشۡتَرُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِي ثَمَنࣰ ا قَلِيلࣰ ا وَإِيَّٰيَ فَٱتَّقُونِ
2:41.en: And believe in what I have sent down confirming that which is [already] with you, and be not the first to disbelieve in it. And do not exchange My signs for a small price, and fear [only] Me

2:42.ar: وَلَا تَلۡبِسُواْ ٱلۡحَقَّ بِٱلۡبَٰطِلِ وَتَكۡتُمُواْ ٱلۡحَقَّ وَأَنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:42.en: And do not mix the truth with falsehood or conceal the truth while you know [it]

2:43.ar: وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱرۡكَعُواْ مَعَ ٱلرَّٰكِعِينَ
2:43.en: And establish prayer and give zakah and bow with those who bow [in worship and obedience]

2:44.ar: ۞أَتَأۡمُرُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ بِٱلۡبِرِّ وَتَنسَوۡنَ أَنفُسَكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ تَتۡلُونَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ
2:44.en: Do you order righteousness of the people and forget yourselves while you recite the Scripture? Then will you not reason

2:45.ar: وَٱسۡتَعِينُواْ بِٱلصَّبۡرِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِۚ وَإِنَّهَا لَكَبِيرَةٌ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلۡخَٰشِعِينَ
2:45.en: And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed, it is difficult except for the humbly submissive [to Allah]

2:46.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُم مُّلَٰقُواْ رَبِّهِمۡ وَأَنَّهُمۡ إِلَيۡهِ رَٰجِعُونَ
2:46.en: Who are certain that they will meet their Lord and that they will return to Him

2:47.ar: يَٰبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَتِيَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنۡعَمۡتُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَأَنِّي فَضَّلۡتُكُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
2:47.en: O Children of Israel, remember My favor that I have bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds

2:48.ar: وَٱتَّقُواْ يَوۡمࣰ ا لَّا تَجۡزِي نَفۡسٌ عَن نَّفۡسࣲ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يُقۡبَلُ مِنۡهَا شَفَٰعَةࣱ وَلَا يُؤۡخَذُ مِنۡهَا عَدۡلࣱ وَلَا هُمۡ يُنصَرُونَ
2:48.en: And fear a Day when no soul will suffice for another soul at all, nor will intercession be accepted from it, nor will compensation be taken from it, nor will they be aided

2:49.ar: وَإِذۡ نَجَّيۡنَٰكُم مِّنۡ ءَالِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ يَسُومُونَكُمۡ سُوٓءَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ يُذَبِّحُونَ أَبۡنَآءَكُمۡ وَيَسۡتَحۡيُونَ نِسَآءَكُمۡۚ وَفِي ذَٰلِكُم بَلَآءࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ عَظِيمࣱ‏
2:49.en: And [recall] when We saved your forefathers from the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted you with the worst torment, slaughtering your [newborn] sons and keeping your females alive. And in that was a great trial from your Lord

2:50.ar: وَإِذۡ فَرَقۡنَا بِكُمُ ٱلۡبَحۡرَ فَأَنجَيۡنَٰكُمۡ وَأَغۡرَقۡنَآ ءَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَأَنتُمۡ تَنظُرُونَ
2:50.en: And [recall] when We parted the sea for you and saved you and drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were looking on

2:51.ar: وَإِذۡ وَٰعَدۡنَا مُوسَىٰٓ أَرۡبَعِينَ لَيۡلَةࣰ ثُمَّ ٱتَّخَذۡتُمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ وَأَنتُمۡ ظَٰلِمُونَ
2:51.en: And [recall] when We made an appointment with Moses for forty nights. Then you took [for worship] the calf after him, while you were wrongdoers

2:52.ar: ثُمَّ عَفَوۡنَا عَنكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٰلِكَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
2:52.en: Then We forgave you after that so perhaps you would be grateful

2:53.ar: وَإِذۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا مُوسَى ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡفُرۡقَانَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَهۡتَدُونَ
2:53.en: And [recall] when We gave Moses the Scripture and criterion that perhaps you would be guided

2:54.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦ يَٰقَوۡمِ إِنَّكُمۡ ظَلَمۡتُمۡ أَنفُسَكُم بِٱتِّخَاذِكُمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ فَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ بَارِئِكُمۡ فَٱقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ عِندَ بَارِئِكُمۡ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡكُمۡۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:54.en: And [recall] when Moses said to his people, "O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves by your taking of the calf [for worship]. So repent to your Creator and kill yourselves. That is best for [all of] you in the sight of your Creator." Then He accepted your repentance; indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful

2:55.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡتُمۡ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ نَرَى ٱللَّهَ جَهۡرَةࣰ فَأَخَذَتۡكُمُ ٱلصَّٰعِقَةُ وَأَنتُمۡ تَنظُرُونَ
2:55.en: And [recall] when you said, "O Moses, we will never believe you until we see Allah outright"; so the thunderbolt took you while you were looking on

2:56.ar: ثُمَّ بَعَثۡنَٰكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَوۡتِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
2:56.en: Then We revived you after your death that perhaps you would be grateful

2:57.ar: وَظَلَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡغَمَامَ وَأَنزَلۡنَا عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلۡوَىٰۖ كُلُواْ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقۡنَٰكُمۡۚ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَٰكِن كَانُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ يَظۡلِمُونَ
2:57.en: And We shaded you with clouds and sent down to you manna and quails, [saying], "Eat from the good things with which We have provided you." And they wronged Us not - but they were [only] wronging themselves

2:58.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا ٱدۡخُلُواْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةَ فَكُلُواْ مِنۡهَا حَيۡثُ شِئۡتُمۡ رَغَدࣰ ا وَٱدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡبَابَ سُجَّدࣰ ا وَقُولُواْ حِطَّةࣱ نَّغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ خَطَٰيَٰكُمۡۚ وَسَنَزِيدُ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
2:58.en: And [recall] when We said, "Enter this city and eat from it wherever you will in [ease and] abundance, and enter the gate bowing humbly and say, 'Relieve us of our burdens.' We will [then] forgive your sins for you, and We will increase the doers of good [in goodness and reward]

2:59.ar: فَبَدَّلَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ قَوۡلًا غَيۡرَ ٱلَّذِي قِيلَ لَهُمۡ فَأَنزَلۡنَا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ رِجۡزࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفۡسُقُونَ
2:59.en: But those who wronged changed [those words] to a statement other than that which had been said to them, so We sent down upon those who wronged a punishment from the sky because they were defiantly disobeying

2:60.ar: ۞وَإِذِ ٱسۡتَسۡقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦ فَقُلۡنَا ٱضۡرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلۡحَجَرَۖ فَٱنفَجَرَتۡ مِنۡهُ ٱثۡنَتَا عَشۡرَةَ عَيۡنࣰ اۖ قَدۡ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسࣲ مَّشۡرَبَهُمۡۖ كُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ مِن رِّزۡقِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا تَعۡثَوۡاْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مُفۡسِدِينَ
2:60.en: And [recall] when Moses prayed for water for his people, so We said, "Strike with your staff the stone." And there gushed forth from it twelve springs, and every people knew its watering place. "Eat and drink from the provision of Allah, and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption

2:61.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡتُمۡ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نَّصۡبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامࣲ وَٰحِدࣲ فَٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخۡرِجۡ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنۢبِتُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ مِنۢ بَقۡلِهَا وَقِثَّآئِهَا وَفُومِهَا وَعَدَسِهَا وَبَصَلِهَاۖ قَالَ أَتَسۡتَبۡدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِي هُوَ أَدۡنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِي هُوَ خَيۡرٌۚ ٱهۡبِطُواْ مِصۡرࣰ ا فَإِنَّ لَكُم مَّا سَأَلۡتُمۡۗ وَضُرِبَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلذِّلَّةُ وَٱلۡمَسۡكَنَةُ وَبَآءُو بِغَضَبࣲ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ يَكۡفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَواْ وَّكَانُواْ يَعۡتَدُونَ
2:61.en: And [recall] when you said, "O Moses, we can never endure one [kind of] food. So call upon your Lord to bring forth for us from the earth its green herbs and its cucumbers and its garlic and its lentils and its onions." [Moses] said, "Would you exchange what is better for what is less? Go into [any] settlement and indeed, you will have what you have asked." And they were covered with humiliation and poverty and returned with anger from Allah [upon them]. That was because they [repeatedly] disbelieved in the signs of Allah and killed the prophets without right. That was because they disobeyed and were [habitually] transgressing

2:67.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأۡمُرُكُمۡ أَن تَذۡبَحُواْ بَقَرَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَتَّخِذُنَا هُزُوࣰ اۖ قَالَ أَعُوذُ بِٱللَّهِ أَنۡ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ
2:67.en: And [recall] when Moses said to his people, "Indeed, Allah commands you to slaughter a cow." They said, "Do you take us in ridicule?" He said, "I seek refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant

2:68.ar: قَالُواْ ٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِيَۚ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةࣱ لَّا فَارِضࣱ وَلَا بِكۡرٌ عَوَانُۢ بَيۡنَ ذَٰلِكَۖ فَٱفۡعَلُواْ مَا تُؤۡمَرُونَ
2:68.en: They said, "Call upon your Lord to make clear to us what it is." [Moses] said, "[Allah] says, 'It is a cow which is neither old nor virgin, but median between that,' so do what you are commanded

2:69.ar: قَالُواْ ٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا لَوۡنُهَاۚ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةࣱ صَفۡرَآءُ فَاقِعࣱ لَّوۡنُهَا تَسُرُّ ٱلنَّٰظِرِينَ
2:69.en: They said, "Call upon your Lord to show us what is her color." He said, "He says, 'It is a yellow cow, bright in color - pleasing to the observers

2:70.ar: قَالُواْ ٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِيَ إِنَّ ٱلۡبَقَرَ تَشَٰبَهَ عَلَيۡنَا وَإِنَّآ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَمُهۡتَدُونَ
2:70.en: They said, "Call upon your Lord to make clear to us what it is. Indeed, [all] cows look alike to us. And indeed we, if Allah wills, will be guided

2:71.ar: قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةࣱ لَّا ذَلُولࣱ تُثِيرُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَلَا تَسۡقِي ٱلۡحَرۡثَ مُسَلَّمَةࣱ لَّا شِيَةَ فِيهَاۚ قَالُواْ ٱلۡـَٰٔنَ جِئۡتَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ فَذَبَحُوهَا وَمَا كَادُواْ يَفۡعَلُونَ
2:71.en: He said, "He says, 'It is a cow neither trained to plow the earth nor to irrigate the field, one free from fault with no spot upon her.' " They said, "Now you have come with the truth." So they slaughtered her, but they could hardly do it

2:74.ar: ثُمَّ قَسَتۡ قُلُوبُكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِيَ كَٱلۡحِجَارَةِ أَوۡ أَشَدُّ قَسۡوَةࣰۚ وَإِنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنۡهُ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُۚ وَإِنَّ مِنۡهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ فَيَخۡرُجُ مِنۡهُ ٱلۡمَآءُۚ وَإِنَّ مِنۡهَا لَمَا يَهۡبِطُ مِنۡ خَشۡيَةِ ٱللَّهِۗ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
2:74.en: Then your hearts became hardened after that, being like stones or even harder. For indeed, there are stones from which rivers burst forth, and there are some of them that split open and water comes out, and there are some of them that fall down for fear of Allah. And Allah is not unaware of what you do

15:87.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَٰكَ سَبۡعࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡمَثَانِي وَٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ ٱلۡعَظِيمَ
15:87.en: And We have certainly given you, [O Muhammad], seven of the often repeated [verses] and the great Qur'an

17:44.ar: تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ ٱلسَّبۡعُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَمَن فِيهِنَّۚ وَإِن مِّن شَيۡءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِهِۦ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تَفۡقَهُونَ تَسۡبِيحَهُمۡۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورࣰ ا
17:44.en: The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is in them exalt Him. And there is not a thing except that it exalts [Allah] by His praise, but you do not understand their [way of] exalting. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving

2:255.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَيُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُۚ لَا تَأۡخُذُهُۥ سِنَةࣱ وَلَا نَوۡمࣱۚ لَّهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يَشۡفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِهِۦۚ يَعۡلَمُ مَا بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَهُمۡۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيۡءࣲ مِّنۡ عِلۡمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَۚ وَسِعَ كُرۡسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَۖ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفۡظُهُمَاۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
2:255.en: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great

2:282.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا تَدَايَنتُم بِدَيۡنٍ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلࣲ مُّسَمࣰّ ى فَٱكۡتُبُوهُۚ وَلۡيَكۡتُب بَّيۡنَكُمۡ كَاتِبُۢ بِٱلۡعَدۡلِۚ وَلَا يَأۡبَ كَاتِبٌ أَن يَكۡتُبَ كَمَا عَلَّمَهُ ٱللَّهُۚ فَلۡيَكۡتُبۡ وَلۡيُمۡلِلِ ٱلَّذِي عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَلۡيَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّهُۥ وَلَا يَبۡخَسۡ مِنۡهُ شَيۡـࣰٔ اۚ فَإِن كَانَ ٱلَّذِي عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡحَقُّ سَفِيهًا أَوۡ ضَعِيفًا أَوۡ لَا يَسۡتَطِيعُ أَن يُمِلَّ هُوَ فَلۡيُمۡلِلۡ وَلِيُّهُۥ بِٱلۡعَدۡلِۚ وَٱسۡتَشۡهِدُواْ شَهِيدَيۡنِ مِن رِّجَالِكُمۡۖ فَإِن لَّمۡ يَكُونَا رَجُلَيۡنِ فَرَجُلࣱ وَٱمۡرَأَتَانِ مِمَّن تَرۡضَوۡنَ مِنَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءِ أَن تَضِلَّ إِحۡدَىٰهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحۡدَىٰهُمَا ٱلۡأُخۡرَىٰۚ وَلَا يَأۡبَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءُ إِذَا مَا دُعُواْۚ وَلَا تَسۡـَٔمُوٓاْ أَن تَكۡتُبُوهُ صَغِيرًا أَوۡ كَبِيرًا إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلِهِۦۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ أَقۡسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَأَقۡوَمُ لِلشَّهَٰدَةِ وَأَدۡنَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَرۡتَابُوٓاْ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَٰرَةً حَاضِرَةࣰ تُدِيرُونَهَا بَيۡنَكُمۡ فَلَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ جُنَاحٌ أَلَّا تَكۡتُبُوهَاۗ وَأَشۡهِدُوٓاْ إِذَا تَبَايَعۡتُمۡۚ وَلَا يُضَآرَّ كَاتِبࣱ وَلَا شَهِيدࣱۚ وَإِن تَفۡعَلُواْ فَإِنَّهُۥ فُسُوقُۢ بِكُمۡۗ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۖ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ ٱللَّهُۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣱ‏
2:282.en: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down. And let a scribe write [it] between you in justice. Let no scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him. So let him write and let the one who has the obligation dictate. And let him fear Allah, his Lord, and not leave anything out of it. But if the one who has the obligation is of limited understanding or weak or unable to dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate in justice. And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men. And if there are not two men [available], then a man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses - so that if one of the women errs, then the other can remind her. And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon. And do not be [too] weary to write it, whether it is small or large, for its [specified] term. That is more just in the sight of Allah and stronger as evidence and more likely to prevent doubt between you, except when it is an immediate transaction which you conduct among yourselves. For [then] there is no blame upon you if you do not write it. And take witnesses when you conclude a contract. Let no scribe be harmed or any witness. For if you do so, indeed, it is [grave] disobedience in you. And fear Allah. And Allah teaches you. And Allah is Knowing of all things

2:285.ar: ءَامَنَ ٱلرَّسُولُ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡهِ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَۚ كُلٌّ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَمَلَٰٓئِكَتِهِۦ وَكُتُبِهِۦ وَرُسُلِهِۦ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيۡنَ أَحَدࣲ مِّن رُّسُلِهِۦۚ وَقَالُواْ سَمِعۡنَا وَأَطَعۡنَاۖ غُفۡرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَإِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
2:285.en: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers, [saying], "We make no distinction between any of His messengers." And they say, "We hear and we obey. [We seek] Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the [final] destination

2:286.ar: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا وُسۡعَهَاۚ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتۡ وَعَلَيۡهَا مَا ٱكۡتَسَبَتۡۗ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذۡنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوۡ أَخۡطَأۡنَاۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحۡمِلۡ عَلَيۡنَآ إِصۡرࣰ ا كَمَا حَمَلۡتَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِنَاۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلۡنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِۦۖ وَٱعۡفُ عَنَّا وَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَٱرۡحَمۡنَآۚ أَنتَ مَوۡلَىٰنَا فَٱنصُرۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:286.en: Allah does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what [good] it has gained, and it will bear [the consequence of] what [evil] it has earned. "Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people

90:4.en: We have certainly created man into hardship

zBPWxXquYtY.speaker: adnan
zBPWxXquYtY.title: A Juz A Day, Juz 1: Submission Without Compromise
zBPWxXquYtY.one_line: Al-Fatihah as the core of the message, then Al-Baqarah's theme of submission without compromise through Adam's repentance and the Israelites and the cow.
zBPWxXquYtY.summary: The presenter opens the series by describing the Quran as guidance, like the animal that leads a herd, which must be understood to be followed. He spends a long stretch on Al-Fatihah as the mother of the book: Allah introduces Himself first through mercy, then praise, then as Master of the Day, so that hope and fear work like a bird's two wings. The shift to You alone we worship turns the surah into a conversation, which is what prayer is; the plural we points to the community, and pairing worship with asking help teaches reliance after effort. The straight path is defined both by where it leads and by who walks it. He presents Al-Baqarah's theme as submission to Allah without compromise and explains the disjointed letters as a call to humility and a sign of the Quran's preservation. The surah describes the best and worst of humanity, invites all people to worship their Lord for reasons it gives, then expects obedience on His terms. A secondary theme is leadership: Adam's khilafah, his slip and repentance, then the Israelites' history of half-hearted obedience, epitomised by the cow they slaughtered only after endless questions, which hardened their hearts. He urges understanding the Quran and submitting fully.

outline.heading: Opening
The Quran as guidance that leads
outline.gist: Huda evokes the animal that leads the herd; we follow with reason and reflection, and following requires understanding.

outline.heading: Interlude
Al-Fatihah: the opener and mother of the book
outline.gist: It carries the crux of the message; al-Razi devotes a whole volume of his tafsir to its single page.

outline.heading: The seven oft-repeated verses
outline.gist: The greatest surah and the first revealed in full, repeated in every prayer.

outline.heading: Every translation is an approximation
outline.gist: He reads Abdul Haleem's translation and adjusts words to convey the meaning better.

outline.heading: Allah introduces Himself through mercy
outline.gist: Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim share the root of mercy: full of mercy, and the one who gives it out.

outline.heading: All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds
outline.gist: All creation praises Him whether or not we join in; mercy is repeated to stress His loving nature.

outline.heading: Master of the Day of Judgment: true justice
outline.gist: Every wronged person and creature gets its day in court.

outline.heading: Hope and fear: the two wings of a bird
outline.gist: Mercy cannot be abused as an excuse; love of Allah and fear of His accountability must stay in balance, and we never despair of His mercy.

outline.heading: You alone we worship: prayer as a conversation
outline.gist: Once we know who Allah is, we find ourselves addressing Him directly, which is what salah is.

outline.heading: We, not I: worship as a community
outline.gist: Actions and accountability are individual, but the ummah prays, fasts and performs Hajj together, bound by love of Allah and His Messenger.

outline.heading: Worship paired with asking for help
outline.gist: True worship is relying on Allah after doing all we can, which builds self-reliance and the will to correct course.

outline.heading: Guide us to the straight path
outline.gist: Bring us onto the road that leads to Jannah and keep us on it until death.

outline.heading: The path defined by who walks it
outline.gist: Religion is practice and also the people of the deen: prophets, companions and heroes who inspire us.

outline.heading: Those who earned anger and those who went astray
outline.gist: A description of the consequences of actions, not a slur: one community angered Musa, the other followed assumption.

outline.heading: Salvific exclusivity
outline.gist: Every religion holds that its path brings salvation, and Muslims need not be ashamed of saying so.

outline.heading: Al-Baqarah: the longest surah and its treasures
outline.gist: It holds the longest verse, Ayat al-Kursi as the greatest verse, and the final two verses that suffice whoever recites them at night.

outline.heading: The first Madinan surah, named after the cow
outline.gist: Revealed after the hijrah, its name comes from the story at verse 67, which ties to its theme.

outline.heading: Theme: submission without compromise
outline.gist: Surah names come from the Prophet, from references or from the companions; this surah's core theme is total submission.

outline.heading: Themes as a scholarly lens, not revelation
outline.gist: Thematic reading is a later, popular approach; other themes can be drawn without contradiction.

outline.heading: Alif Lam Mim: the humility to accept
outline.gist: Allah did not tell us their meaning; accepting that is the prerequisite humility for receiving guidance.

outline.heading: The disjointed letters as proof of preservation
outline.gist: Everyone pronounces them as separate letters, showing the Quran was preserved in recitation as well as writing.

outline.heading: Guidance for the mindful: the traits of believers
outline.gist: Belief in the unseen, prayer, giving, belief in all revelation and certainty of the Hereafter; anyone with these traits earns the title.

outline.heading: Al-Baqarah answers Al-Fatihah's prayer
outline.gist: We asked to be guided, and the next surah opens with here is the guidance.

outline.heading: Sealed hearts: the worst case, not every disbeliever
outline.gist: It describes those who have made up their minds against any evidence; those in between are invited to the path.

outline.heading: O people, worship your Lord who created you
outline.gist: All humanity is invited, with reasons: He created us and sustains life through earth, sky and rain, so set up no rivals.

outline.heading: Submission on Allah's terms
outline.gist: Allah gives reasons to submit, but once understood, worship is on His terms, as prayer times show.

outline.heading: The challenge to produce a surah
outline.gist: Those who think it man-made cannot match it; the fire awaits the obstinate.

outline.heading: Gardens graced with flowing streams
outline.gist: Mercy follows mention of punishment; water and greenery, prized even here, picture a place of bliss in a life of toil.

outline.heading: Familiar-looking fruit, unlike anything here
outline.gist: The food resembles worldly food so it is not unsettling, but is pure and beyond imagination.

outline.heading: Bliss with no fear of losing it
outline.gist: Pure spouses, no rancour, and no anxiety that the good will be taken away: what we are working toward.

outline.heading: How can you disbelieve? Life, death and return
outline.gist: Everyone knows they came from nothing and will die; the believer adds the return for accountability.

outline.heading: Earth for you, and seven heavens
outline.gist: The earth was made for us as custodians, not exploiters; our final home is where Adam was created.

outline.heading: A second theme: leadership
outline.gist: Adam is leadership begun, the Israelites leadership gone wrong (2:40-123), and Ibrahim exemplary leadership (from 2:124).

outline.heading: The angels ask about a successor on earth
outline.gist: They question to understand, not to challenge, which the religion welcomes; Allah knows what they do not.

outline.heading: Adam taught the names: the human potential for good
outline.gist: The capacity to learn means human good, when united on guidance, outweighs the evil the angels foresaw.

outline.heading: Learning is what makes us human
outline.gist: When we stop learning, part of our humanity withers; believers should keep learning about everything good.

outline.heading: The slip from the garden
outline.gist: Weakness exacerbated by Satan's whispering causes us to fall from a state of bliss.

outline.heading: Repentance can raise one higher than before
outline.gist: The expectation is not sinlessness but returning to Allah and trying to be better.

outline.heading: O Children of Israel: an appeal to their lineage
outline.gist: Israel is a prophet's name; reminding them they descend from prophets appeals to the good in them, whatever the modern state does.

outline.heading: Honour your pledge and do not be the first to disbelieve
outline.gist: Invitation comes before reminder: believe, do not sell the verses cheaply or hide the truth, and pray with those who pray.

outline.heading: Remember when: a history of blessings
outline.gist: Rescue from Pharaoh, the parted sea and the scripture, met with the calf and demands to see Allah.

outline.heading: Compromise at every turn
outline.gist: Complaining about manna was not about food but about refusing full submission.

outline.heading: Humiliation from half-submission
outline.gist: Persistent rejection and transgression brought humiliation and Allah's wrath.

outline.heading: The cow: questions instead of obedience
outline.gist: Any cow would have done; asking about age, colour and type is the attitude of someone who does not want to comply.

outline.heading: Why the surah is named after the cow
outline.gist: They obeyed while dragging their feet, almost as if they had not, losing the blessings that come with obedience.

outline.heading: Hearts as hard as rock
outline.gist: Continual compromise in the relationship with Allah leaves the heart closed to anything entering it.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Submission without compromise
themes.note: Al-Baqarah's theme: Allah gives reasons to submit, then expects obedience on His terms.

themes.label: Submission without compromise
themes.note: The Israelites' repeated half-obedience, culminating in the cow, hardened their hearts.

themes.label: Allah's mercy and justice
themes.note: Al-Fatihah introduces Allah through mercy, praise and judgment; hope and fear are the believer's two wings.

themes.label: Prayer as conversation
themes.note: Al-Fatihah turns from describing Allah to addressing Him; worship is collective and joined with seeking His help.

themes.label: The Quran
themes.note: The Quran as guidance to be understood; Al-Fatihah as its crux; translations as approximations.

themes.label: Leadership
themes.note: Adam's khilafah and his potential for good through learning, framed against the Israelites and Ibrahim.

themes.label: Tawbah
themes.note: Adam's slip and repentance show the human pattern and that repentance can raise one's station.

themes.label: Learning
themes.note: Learning is inherently human and should be constant.

themes.label: Paradise
themes.note: Gardens with flowing streams, familiar yet unimaginable food, and bliss without fear of loss.
